picks.blurb: The Kennesaw State Owls (1-4, 0-1 CUSA) won this league last year and were expected to contend for the title again, but they've had a disappointing start to the year and have dropped back-to-back one-score games. Most recently, they lost 27-26 to Jacksonville State in their league opener. The Missouri State Bears (1-4, 0-1 CUSA), meanwhile, were a surprising bowl team last year in their first season at the FBS level. However, with a new coaching staff this season, they've struggled and are still looking for their first FBS win. Missouri State's injury report entering CUSA game against Delaware - AOL Skip to main content Advertisement Dulles T..., VA Dulles Town Center, VA Local News Menu 24/7 Help For premium support please call: Sign in Mail 24/7 Help For premium support please call: Missouri State's injury report entering CUSA game against Delaware Liam Keating, Springfield News-Leader Thu, October 15, 2026 at 10:11 PM UTC 0 SPRINGFIELD — There’s little time to dwell and celebrate Missouri State’s win over Kennesaw State on Wednesday, Oct. 14. The Bears (2-4, 1-1 in CUSA) are moving on to its next Conference USA clash against Delaware (2-4, 0-2) on Tuesday, Oct. 20. Against the Owls, Missouri State was without three key players on the offensive side of the ball. Missouri State was down three starters in running back Breezy Dubar, offensive lineman Ryan Mitchell and wide receiver Mekhi Miller. “Two guys are concussion guys that I expect we get back this week being Breezy and Ryan,” Woods said. Missouri State: Casey Woods pushes for more Group of Six representation in expanded CFP Missouri State: Jmariyae Robinson one step closer to the triple crown As for Miller, the fifth-year player suffered an injury during pregame warmups against Kennesaw State. Woods does not know the extent of the injury as of Thursday, Oct. 15. “Mekhi had a weird thing come up pregame,” Woods said. “We are still doing some more. I don’t have enough information to get you exactly what’s going on with that right now.” Dubar has rushed for 218 yards, which ranks second-best on the team. He’s also tied with Ramone Green Jr. with two touchdowns for the most on the roster. Mitchell featured on the offensive line in every game before missing the last game. Miller is Missouri State’s third-best wide receiver option. He has 13 catches for 146 yards. Liam Keating covers high school sports and Missouri State athletics for The Springfield News-Leader. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 4 Ohio State is looking for revenge against No. 5 Indiana after last year's Big Ten title game Getty Images The 100th all-time meeting between Ohio State and Indiana is shaping up to be an epic game. The No. 5 Hoosiers play host to the fourth-ranked Buckeyes with their undefeated record on the line. The winner will have the inside track to the Big Ten Championshiop Game in Indianapolis The reigning national champion, Indiana, hasn't faced a single ranked team, and it's had one of the easier schedules in the Big Ten. The Hoosiers did get a dicey road test against Nebraska last weekend, but that was a nice warm-up for what's to come on Saturday. Despite losing a number of key pieces from last year's team, Indiana still looks like a serious title contender thanks to newcomers Nick Marsh (528 receiving yards and six touchdowns), Turbo Richard (leads Big Ten in rushing yards) and Tobi Osunsanmi (leads the Big Ten in sacks and tackles for loss). Ohio State will be looking for a little revenge after losing to Indiana in the 2025 Big Ten Championship. That loss snapped the Buckeyes' 30-game winning streak over the Hoosiers, so they'll try to start a new one on Saturday. That's entirely possible, largely due to the presence of Heisman Trophy favorite and athletic anomaly Jeremiah Smith , who leads the conference in just about every major receiving category. This is one of the best games on a loaded Week 7 slate, so here is everything you must know as No. 5 Indiana visits No. 4 Ohio State. Where to watch Ohio State vs. Indiana live Date : Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Memorial Stadium -- Bloomington, Indiana TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Ohio State vs. Indiana: Need to know Annual top-five matchup: For the first 97 meetings between these teams, there were zero top-five matchups. When the game kicks off Saturday, it will be the third time in as many years that Indiana and Ohio State have played with both teams ranked inside the top five. If we're honest, Indiana was the main reason there were no top-five matchups in the first 97 meetings, but that has changed in a big way now. The Hoosiers have the resources and the coach to compete with the Buckeyes, so we may have a budding Big Ten rivalry on our hands. Smith's historic season: Every week, Smith rewrites the record books at the program, conference and NCAA level. That could continue on Saturday because Smith is just one receiving touchdown shy of matching Michigan legend Braylon Edwards for the most in Big Ten history (39). Smith has already secured the school records for career receptions (211), receiving yards (3,474) and receiving touchdowns (38). He should only add to those totals against a Hoosiers secondary Smith beat for 144 yards last year. Sacking Sayin: One way to make sure Smith never gets the football is to hit Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin while he still has the ball. That's exactly what the Hoosiers did in the Big Ten title game, sacking Sayin five times. Indiana has the personnel to get after Sayin again this time around. Osunsanmi and Stephen Daley have combined for 10 sacks, and Ohio State has allowed 11 sacks of Sayin thus far. The battle between the Indiana defensive front and the Ohio State offensive line in pass protection will be critical. Ohio State vs. Indiana prediction, picks This should be another tremendous game between a pair of national title contenders, and it may very well be a preview of the Big Ten Championship matchup. Having said that, I do wonder how well Indiana's passing defense will hold up for 60 minutes, especially without D'Angelo Ponds in the secondary this time. Ohio State hits enough big plays with Smith to create some breathing room late. This 2026 matchup should be more of the same – if not an even more dominant showing from the Hoosiers’ pass-rushing attack. Halfway through the regular season, Sayin has already been sacked 11 times. And Indiana has a whopping 20 sacks in six games. The writing is on the wall – in Sharpie. Expect the Hoosiers to apply a lot of pressure on Sayin. It’ll be interesting to see how Sayin responds, especially considering he’s shown off his legs more often this year (and Indiana has been vulnerable to QBs who take off). It has put up at least 31 points in every league game thus far. Sayin and stud wide receiver Jeremiah Smith have been flat-out unstoppable. As for the Hoosiers, they have scored at least 20 in every outing in 2026. Then again, Indiana scored six points through three quarters last Saturday at Nebraska. And, on the flip side, Ohio State hasn’t seen a defense half as sturdy as Indiana’s, aside from Texas, which held the Buckeyes to only three points in the second half. If Indiana’s defense strings together four full quarters, it can bottle up this Ohio State offense – or at least keep it at bay (Smith won’t be entirely shut down by any defense this year). And the expectation is that the Hoosiers offense, which has sputtered at times this year, struggles with this Buckeyes defense. It’d be a surprise to see either team score three touchdowns. Indiana, which is holding opponents to a Big Ten best 75.0 rushing yards per game, has been an absolute brick wall against the run. Ohio State, meanwhile, hasn’t exactly been running through anybody. It managed just 94 rushing yards against Texas in Week 2. Kent State held the Buckeyes to 3.8 yards per carry. You get the idea. In general, Ohio State’s experienced offensive line has been surprisingly uninspiring in 2026. Expect Indiana’s elite defensive front to have its way getting after Sayin and stifling the run game. But can the Hoosiers do enough against Smith? That will be the question. picks.headline: Ohio State On SI Staff Picks: Can Buckeyes Get Revenge on Indiana in Week 7?
picks.blurb: Ohio State On SI Staff Picks: Can Buckeyes Get Revenge on Indiana in Week 7? Skip to main content SI.COM 2025 Football Bracket Buckeyes In the NFL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES BB This game needs no introduction. Some may argue this is the game Ohio State has been preparing fo r all season long . Now it has a chance to go to Indiana and rewrite a wrong from last December, when it lost the Big Ten Championship game to the Hoosiers, which ultimately led to them completing their undefeated season. Ohio State isn’t undefeated like Indiana is. However, the Buckeyes are rolling through the start of the Big Ten schedule without any real hiccups. Ohio State (5-1, 3-0 Big Ten) has had this game against the Hoosiers (6-0, 3-0 Big Ten) earmarked on the schedule since it was released. So much so that both teams have remained the class of the Big Ten all year long, with a possible elimination scenario in play come December, ahead of the Big Ten title game in Indianapolis. Someone’s supremacy must be disrupted . Will the Buckeyes struggle again, or will the Hoosiers exploit their weaknesses? Check out our staff picks as the game gets underway. Ohio State vs. Indiana Week 7 Outlook Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day watches during the NCAA football game against the Maryland Terrapins at Ohio Stadium in Columbus on Oct. 10, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: noon ET/9 a.m. PT TV Channel: FOX (consult TV Guide or preferred streaming provider for details). Odds: Ohio State -3; over/under is 50.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Location : Memorial Stadium – Bloomington, Ind. Ohio State’s record under Ryan Day : 87-13 (8-6 in postseason bowl games/CFP). Last time vs. Indiana: A 13-10 loss in the Big Ten title game in a top-two showdown. Ohio State leads the series dating back to 1989, 31-1-1. Pregame festivities: Big Noon Kickoff will be there. Ohio State so far this season: 5-1 (3-0 Big Ten) Zain Bando: 6-0 Dylan Buganski : 5-1 Rafael Zamorano : 4-1 (no pick in Week 6 nor Week 7) Chip Minnich : 4-0 (began contributing ahead of Week 3) Zain Bando: Ohio State 28, Indiana 24 There is no such thing as a one-game season, but the Buckeyes may beg to differ. Indiana handed Ohio State one of its two back-to-back losses to end last season and now, on a fall Saturday in Bloomington, the entire year could come down to whether Ohio State can finally sneak up and regain head-to-head dominance and steal a road win. If wideout Jeremiah Smith gets space and gets comfortable thanks to Julian Sayin, and forces the defense to tire Hoosiers quarterback Josh Hoover, the game could easily deliver a fantastic finish in the closing minutes. We’ll see if the Buckeyes can make it interesting, or better yet, secure a road win that could change the season for good. Chip Minnich: Ohio State 31, Indiana 28 The highly anticipated, top-five Big Ten showdown between the Ohio State Buckeyes on Saturday hinges on how Ryan Day's squad handles sudden depth issues against an elite Indiana defense. Ohio State faces an uphill battle following a troubling availability report ruling out two of the team's most relied-upon members on offense ~ Austin Siereveld and Ja'Kobi Jackson. With Austin Siereveld missing his second straight game, the loss of the Preseason All-Big Ten selection strips the Buckeyes of their offensive line leader. This forces Gabe VanSickle and right tackle Phillip Daniels into hyper-extended roles against a vicious Hoosier pass rush; Daniels has not played since the loss at Texas on September 12th. Ja'Kobi Jackson, the team's powerhouse short-yardage back and touchdown leader (6 TDs), is sidelined with a surprise ankle injury. While Bo Jackson will shoulder the primary workload, Ja'Kobi Jackson's absence eliminates the physical lightning-and-thunder dynamic Ohio State uses to control the tempo. Could Isaiah West, who missed a key block that led to a pick-six interception in last week's Maryland game, get a chance at redemption? West offers a physical style of play comparable to Ja'Kobi Jackson. The fans who have been clamoring for Legend Bey may see Bey as a larger part of the offensive game plan. Ohio State offensive coordinator Arthur Smith will need to be creative in the run game and involve other receiving talents beyond Jeremiah Smith. With a depleted ground game and a reshuffled protection unit, the entire game plan in my estimation rests on the shoulders of junior quarterback Julian Sayin. Sayin has been using his legs to gain positive yardage in recent games and may need to run more frequently than desired by Sayin or the Ohio State coaching staff. The Ohio State defense is going to be tested, as Indiana boasts talented wide receivers in Nick Marsh and Charlie Becker, plus a strong running game led by Turbo Richard. Quarterback Josh Hoover has not yet thrown an interception this season, so perhaps Ohio State defensive coordinator Matt Patricia will be able to scheme some situations that result in a turnover. Expect a classic, physical Big Ten chess match. While Indiana enters the match healthier and with a strong defensive front, Sayin's elite talent and postseason poise will provide just enough explosive plays in a late two-minute drill to secure a tight, field-goal victory for the Buckeyes in Bloomington. Dylan Buganski: Ohio State 24, Indiana 17 There may not be a matchup this team as well as fans circled coming into this season then the rematch of last year’s Big Ten Championship game in what may be Indiana’s biggest home game in program history. There are old and new faces on both sides, and the clash between head coaches Ryan Day and Curt Cignetti may become one of the conference’s greatest rivalries going forward. Ohio State comes into this matchup battle-tested, seeing ranked teams Iowa and Texas on the road and finishing 1-1 in those matchups. This will be Indiana’s first ranked matchup of the season, but they had a comeback victory at Nebraska last week, in which the Cornhuskers should probably have been a ranked team. This matchup will come down to how dominant Indiana can be at the line of scrimmage, as that may be the only position where Indiana may have more talent than the Buckeyes, other than maybe running back. Indiana should be able to run the ball decently and stop the run on the other side. At the end of the day, the secondary for Ohio State should limit the passing game from exploding and another weapon in the passing game has a big game next to Smith, inching Ohio State to a win in this matchup and moving what we may call in 10 years the “Cignetti-Day War” to a 2-1 Buckeye lead. picks.blurb: Rece Davis Reveals Ohio State-Indiana Pick for 'Biggest Game' in Bloomington History Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN College GameDay host Rece Davis picked Ohio State to win at Indiana on Saturday, siding with the Buckeyes in a top-five showdown that puts the Hoosiers’ 22-game winning streak on the line in Bloomington. On the College GameDay podcast, Davis joined fellow panelists Pete Thamel and Dan Wetzel in taking No. 4 Ohio State (5-1) over No. 5 Indiana (6-0), though he expects a close finish. “I think a field goal at the end decides it one way or the other,” Davis said. Rece Davis explains his Ohio State pick Ohio State head coach Ryan Day takes the team out of the tunnel before the game against the Maryland Terrapins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis called Saturday’s noon ET kickoff on Fox the “ biggest game in the history of Bloomington , Indiana, not played on a basketball court.” It’s a rematch of last December’s Big Ten championship game, which Indiana won 13-10 in Indianapolis on its way to the national title. Davis called Saturday’s noon ET kickoff on Fox the “ biggest game in the history of Bloomington , Indiana, not played on a basketball court.” It’s a rematch of last December’s Big Ten championship game, which Indiana won 13-10 in Indianapolis on its way to the national title. His case against the Hoosiers rests on the streak itself. “When you have a winning streak as long as Indiana’s, longest in the country ... you start having these near misses,” Davis said. “Sooner or later, one gets you, and it can almost reset you a little bit.” Indiana held off Northwestern 29-23 in its Big Ten opener after starting running back Turbo Richard left with an injury, leaning on backup Lee Beebe Jr. for 203 rushing yards. Last Saturday in Lincoln, Indiana trailed Nebraska 17-6 in the fourth quarter before quarterback Josh Hoover hit receiver Nick Marsh for touchdowns of 75 and 44 yards, the second on fourth-and-1. Afterward, Indiana coach Curt Cignetti said his players “ took a deep breath and relaxed and forgot all the garbage in the first half.” Can Ohio State protect Julian Sayin? Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin (10) throws during the college football game against the Maryland Terrapins | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Davis pointed to the Buckeyes’ offensive line as the deciding matchup. “Ohio State has allowed pressure on 27% of its dropbacks this season. That’s 14th in the Big Ten,” Davis said. “That’s not a great formula against Indiana. Indiana does an unbelievable job of getting pressure without blitzing.” Davis pointed to the Buckeyes’ offensive line as the deciding matchup. “Ohio State has allowed pressure on 27% of its dropbacks this season. That’s 14th in the Big Ten,” Davis said. “That’s not a great formula against Indiana. Indiana does an unbelievable job of getting pressure without blitzing.” Indiana leads the Big Ten with 20 sacks, while Ohio State has allowed 11, which ranks 14th in the conference . The Hoosiers also finished last December’s 13-10 win with five sacks and nine tackles for loss. Still, the Buckeyes have done damage when the pocket holds. Quarterback Julian Sayin, who holds No. 1 in our Big Ten quarterback rankings , has thrown for 1,772 yards and 17 touchdowns, and wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has 916 receiving yards and 11 touchdown catches. Ohio State’s offense also ranks second nationally in expected points added per pass, while Indiana’s defense ranks 76th in that measure. And the Buckeyes’ line landed on the Joe Moore Award midseason honor roll on Wednesday. Why Davis still backs Indiana’s offense Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover (10) passes against the Nebraska Cornhuskers | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis pushed back on the idea that Indiana’s attack has slipped, comparing Hoover to Fernando Mendoza, who quarterbacked the Hoosiers to last season’s title. Davis pushed back on the idea that Indiana’s attack has slipped, comparing Hoover to Fernando Mendoza, who quarterbacked the Hoosiers to last season’s title. “If Josh Hoover plays 16 games, as Fernando did last year, the numbers are going to be pretty much the same, almost the same,” Davis said. “He’s thrown 17 touchdown passes. I think Fernando finished with 41 last year. You double that to the end of the season, you’re at 34, and then you have the playoff.” Davis also noted that Indiana remains a run-first team. “Turbo Richard leads the conference in runs of 20 yards or longer,” he said. “They average over six yards a carry.” He placed the matchup in rare Big Ten company, too. “Only once have two teams played three consecutive seasons and been in the top five of the AP poll in all three meetings: Michigan and Ohio State in the middle of the legendary Ten-Year War between Bo Schembechler and Woody Hayes,” Davis said. ESPN analyst Greg McElroy took the opposite side this week, picking Indiana as the underdog to extend its streak to 23 games. away.headline: Ohio State football releases first injury report vs. Indiana: Who’s in, who’s out for the Buckeyes

away.headline: Ohio State announces injury update on quarterback Julian Sayin
away.blurb: Starting quarterback Julian Sayin was knocked out of the game with a forearm injury after taking a massive hit from the pocket. He later returned to the sideline with his arm in a sling. After the game, Ohio State head coach Ryan Day announced that Sayin would be out for “several weeks.” Ohio State held on to win after Indiana wide receiver Nick Marsh stepped out of bounds on what could’ve been a game-winning touchdown pass late in the fourth quarter. Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover had Marsh open, but he was barely out of bounds, giving Ohio State the win. Ohio State notched a massive win over Indiana on Saturday, but it came at a cost. MORE: College football games on today, Week 7 AP Top 25 TV schedule for Saturday Sayin finished the game with 235 yards through the air, two touchdowns, and two interceptions. Freshman quarterback Luke Fahey replaced him and didn’t complete a pass. What happened after Sayin got hurt? The loss snapped Indiana’s 22-game winning streak since the program went undefeated last year and was 6-0 at the start of this season. Who replaces Sayin going forward? The favorite to start is Fahey, a three-star recruit in the 2026 recruiting class, per 247Sports Composite rankings . He was the No. 586 overall recruit in the country before enrolling at Ohio State. Ohio State is 6-1 overall and will play USC in its next game on Halloween after a bye week next weekend. We’ll see if Sayin can make his way back to the lineup before the end of the season.

"Fahey is one of the most talented quarterbacks out West," Biggins wrote. "He's surgical from the pocket and can pick a defense a part with his accuracy and timing. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Covers custom image. Florida and Texas square off in a high-stakes SEC showdown Saturday, with both programs looking to bounce back from disappointing losses. The Gators have dropped two straight, including a lopsided defeat to South Carolina, while the Longhorns are looking to regroup after falling to rival Oklahoma and surrendering their No. 1 ranking. Our Florida vs. Texas prediction backs the Longhorns to cover the 10.5-point spread, but our college football expert sees even better value in the game total. Read on for our analysis and more college football picks for Saturday's slate. Who will win Florida vs Texas: Texas -10.5 Have the Florida Gators been "figured out"? I'm not sure. Has Florida had extreme regression over the last few games and probably gotten to a record it should be, even if it required some extremely unbalanced games to do so? Probably so. I'm taking the Texas Longhorns to cover this -10.5 number; it's a small edge, and I wouldn't play it past here. Florida's offense is (still) legit, ranking 8th in EPA per pass, but the defense has been a sieve. The Gators rank 123rd in success rate allowed (49.7%) and dead last at 136th in 3rd/4th down success allowed, so Texas doesn't need to be explosive to sustain drives. They need to be solid, which is pretty much the definition of an Arch Manning-led offense. On the other side, the Longhorns' defense ranks 2nd nationally in adjusted EPA per play, 9th against the run and 11th against the pass, while allowing just 29.9% of available yards (5th) . Florida won't trade scores all afternoon. I'll lay it. TOP PICK Florida vs Texas Over/Under pick: Under 51.5 I'm playing the Under 51.5 and would take it down to 50.5 (50%). It's my top pick. Florida's offense has been efficient, but it hasn't faced a defense that controls early downs as Texas does. The Longhorns rank 5th nationally in early-down EPA per play allowed, which has opponents facing an average 3rd down distance of 8.12 yards , 15th in the country. Florida already ranks 105th in average 3rd down distance at 7.62 yards , so expect a lot of long-yardage situations and stalled drives. Texas also ranks 6th in defensive EPA per drive, so even when the Gators move the ball, points haven't come easily against this unit. The Texas offense isn't built to push this total either. It ranks 55th in success rate and 67th in EPA per pass, and gains just 46.5% of available yards (70th). Expect the Longhorns to win with long, methodical drives that drain the clock rather than quick-strike scores. Florida vs Texas combo This combo is built around one game script: Florida hangs around early, then Texas takes over. Coming off two straight blowouts, the Gators should come out with urgency, and an offense that ranks 8th in EPA per pass can keep them close for a half. Texas's offense isn't built to jump out to fast leads either. The second half is where the Longhorns' advantages show up. Florida's defense ranks dead last in 3rd-and-4th down success allowed, and long Texas drives should wear the Gators down, pull away on the scoreboard, and eat clock to keep this under the total. Florida 1st Half +6.5 Florida vs Texas prop: Florida Under 2.5 touchdowns Florida has been able to move the ball this season, but finishing drives against this Texas defense is a different story. The Longhorns hold opponents to a 38.8% passing success rate (25th) and rank 6th in defensive EPA per drive, so even productive Gators possessions are likely to stall short of the end zone. With Texas expected to control the ball on long drives, Florida's opportunities will be limited, and field goals are the more likely outcome when it does get into scoring range. Coming off a loss, Texas is eager to get back in the conference title picture with a good showing against the reeling Gators. Here's what you need to know heading into the matchup as The Big Lead locks in our final prediction for this Week 7 college football clash. Texas offensive inconsistency and defensive strength Arch Manning has shown flashes but has been uneven against better competition, with turnovers becoming a recurring issue. Pass protection has been mixed despite solid grades in some metrics, and the run game has lacked consistent explosiveness. Where Texas separates itself is on defense. The unit ranks among the better groups nationally in yards allowed and has been especially effective limiting yards after contact. Rushing off the edges and overall tackling efficiency have been strengths. That could create some real problems for a Florida offense that has looked worn down. Defensive collapse, run game issues at Florida NCAA Football: Mississippi at Florida Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Even during the Gators' win streak, critics sounded the alarm about this defense. The two-game skid has confirmed those worries. Missed tackles and coverage breakdowns have piled up? The total damage? Florida is the SEC's worst defense in total output, explosive plays allowed, and against the pass. It's the second-worst in scoring. On offense, the Florida run game that once looked dominant has been largely shut down by better fronts. Jadan Baugh's production has dropped sharply. After rushing for over 130 yards in four wins, his totals fell to 13 and then 59 yards in two losses. Questions also linger about quarterback availability with Aaron Philo listed as questionable. A potential shift to Tramell Jones Jr. would add even more uncertainty against a Texas defense that flies to the ball. Key matchup dynamics to watch Texas holds clear edges in defensive structure and home-field stability. Florida's ability to create explosive plays through play-action and yards after catch remains a theoretical strength, but recent film shows those opportunities drying up against disciplined units. Scheme-wise, Texas' ability to limit perimeter runs and finish tackles aligns poorly with what Florida has relied on. Manning should face less pressure than he did against Oklahoma, giving him cleaner looks against a secondary that has been vulnerable. Florida vs. Texas prediction: Who wins and why? Texas is the more complete team right now, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. Even with offensive questions, the Longhorns' ability to control the line of scrimmage and force Florida into obvious passing situations should decide the game. Florida has the talent to keep stretches competitive, but the recent defensive regression and limited run game make a full road upset unlikely. The Big Lead Prediction: Texas 31, Florida 17

The Florida Gators are in a rough spot at 4-2 as they head to Austin to take on the Texas Longhorns on Saturday afternoon. After two blowout losses to the Missouri Tigers and South Carolina Gamecocks on homecoming, Jon Sumrall 's team is in a tough spot. They were at one point being talked about as potentially being the 2019 LSU Tigers from on the precipice of collapsing. It's his first year at the helm, and the talent level still isn't quite there yet. For the Longhorns, they have beaten Ohio State, but are coming off a tough loss in the Red River Rivalry to the Oklahoma Sooners. They are in an interesting spot right now, and a win is a must for both teams. Who will get the win? Our experts made their predictions. Texas 38, Florida 24 Can we trust the Florida Gators? Honestly, no, and that includes the four-game winning streak to start the season with a massive blowout win over Ole Miss. The defense is struggling to generate pressure and the coverage on the back end has been incredibly inconsistent. Even with Texas having lost Red River last week, their success so far this season and offensive talent gets the Longhorns the win. Can the Gators get the win? Absolutely! Will they? I doubt it. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida Texas 33, Florida 19 Both teams come in off dismal losses to unranked teams. The Longhorns, who haven't looked dominant this year by any means, gagged away a game they should have won against Oklahoma but for a pick six and a punt block touchdown. Florida got mollywhopped by South Carolina one game after getting throttled by Missouri. As such, it's tough to tell up from down with these two teams. But my mind immediately goes to two things. First, the Horns' front is still nasty, and Florida suddenly can't find any space for Jadan Baugh and the ground game. On the other side, Florida's defense has become a sieve, and I don't trust they've found a way to fix it yet. Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo are too much for the Longhorns, who win comfortably in Austin. – Craig Smith , A to Z Miami Texas 31, Florida 20 Arch Manning has faced plenty of criticism for his inconsistency this season, but this is the type of matchup that could help him get back on track. Florida's pass defense has been a major weakness, and I expect Manning to take full advantage by delivering his best performance of the 2026 season. The Longhorns have the talent to exploit the Gators' struggling secondary, and Manning should find plenty of opportunities to push the ball downfield and put points on the board. After an uneven stretch offensively, this could be the breakthrough performance Texas needs. Florida should have some success early, particularly with running back Jadan Baugh leading the way. Baugh has been one of the Gators' most productive playmakers, and I expect him to help Florida move the ball and keep the game competitive in the first half. However, Texas has the defensive talent to make adjustments and limit Florida's offensive production as the game progresses. The Gators have struggled to maintain consistency in recent weeks, and that issue will catch up with them again in Austin. Texas pulls away in the second half, with Manning and the offense doing enough to secure a much-needed win. – Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame Texas 21, Florida 17 The Gators have fallen off a bit in the last few weeks after starting red hot. Texas is coming off a disappointing loss to Oklahoma. So, you know, Steve Sarkisian is going to be looking to get his team rolling again. Last week probably showed Texas what they should be doing more often on offense. They need to run more quick-game stuff with Arch Manning, because the long, developing routes downfield aren't helping the offense. Their offensive line isn't great, so they need to start running more quick-game plays. I think this past game showed some of that, and Texas still gets the win despite the offense struggling against a decent Florida defense. – Justin Churchill , A to Z Oklahoma Texas 30, Florida 20 As high as I was on the Florida Gators after the Ole Miss win, that hype has come crashing down after games against Missouri and South Carolina. The offense, led by Jadan Baugh, simply hasn't looked the same, and now the availability of starting QB Aaron Philo is in question. As for Texas, the Longhorns are coming off an embarrassing loss of their own after losing Red River to a bad OU team, and they aim to get back on track. Florida's defense has been bad, to say the least, and this game may serve as a great game for Arch Manning nd Texas. Give me the Longhorns here. – Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama Texas 28, Florida 17 Texas and Florida both need wins this week, and the pressure is even higher for Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning. Two losses for Texas at this point in the season would make things very uncomfortable in Austin, and perhaps it would mark the beginning of the end for some important names there. I don't think that's going to happen, though. I think Texas bounces back this week behind a strong defensive performance and looks the part against Florida. If the Longhorns can limit Jaden Baugh, they'll defend home field without much issue. I think Florida hangs around, but the Longhorns put it away in the fourth quarter. – Brandon Little , A to Z Ohio State Final Prediction for Florida vs. Texas It shouldn't be much of a surprise that none of our experts have picked the Gators, as they have lost our trust after the disastrous performances of the last two weeks. A win here would do wonders to get them back in our good graces. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. picks.headline: Gators Legend Chris Doering Predicts 'Nasty' Gators vs. No. 7 Longhorns Outcome
picks.blurb: Gators Legend Chris Doering Predicts 'Nasty' Gators vs. No. 7 Longhorns Outcome - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NBA Predictions World Series schedule Week 7 Waiver Wire 49ers are 6-0 Reese, Dream get even For the Gators to upset Texas, they're going to need a big day from running back Jadan Baugh. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Scott Kennedy Sat, October 17, 2026 at 12:41 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Florida Gators take on the No. 7 Texas Longhorns on Saturday at Noon EST . The Gators will be eager to return to the field after a pair of less-than-stellar performances the last two weeks. Head coach Jon Sumrall admitted earlier this week that he was taking a more hands-on approach to making sure his players understood what it meant to play Florida Gators football. They'll also be giving second-year quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. his first start after seeing mop-up duty the last two weeks. Gators legend Chris Doering appeared on the Paul Finebaum show to preview the Gators at Longhorns, and he was having flashbacks from the last time Florida traveled to Austin. "For whatever reason, I cannot get the idea or the memory of watching Scott Strickland on the sideline two years ago, last time that Florida went to Austin, and I think they were down 42-0 in the first half and 11:00 a.m. (Central) start," Doering said on the show . Doering was off by a touchdown. It was 35-0 en route to a 49-17 Texas win. However, the kickoff time isn't the only similarity Doering points out. Florida started a backup quarterback two years ago as well. "They were without their starting quarterback. Maybe his mobility can help going up against probably the best front seven that they will face the entire season," Doering said of Jones. Sumrall was unhappy with how the Gators played on the lines of scrimmage in their two losses, and Doering is afraid that won't be fixed quickly enough to beat a powerful Longhorns team. "The blueprint's out on beating Florida. It's being able to out-physical them on the line of scrimmage, being able to stop the run. Everything starts with the run game for Florida. Then the secondary is incredibly porous. Something that we were afraid of in the offseason is now coming to light. "Teams are being able to take advantage of it the last couple of weeks, including last week with LaNorris Sellers converted, I think, about five or six 3rd and 10 pluses." Sellers was an incredibly efficient 23 of 35 passing for 279 yards and four touchdowns in the Gamecocks' 38-19 win. They were 10 for 16 overall on third down. Texas managed 382 yards against Oklahoma last week, but they only scored 24 points in the 27-24 loss to the Sooners. Tennessee held them to 262 yards and 20 points in the previous game. Doering thinks this could be the week the Longhorn offense breaks out. "So, I feel like Texas, if you ever wanted a slump buster, this is it for Texas's offense. I think it's going to get nasty, unfortunately, there in Austin. I think Texas wins by multiple touchdowns," Doering finished. The Longhorns present a big challenge to the Gators, but that also means it's a big opportunity to get back into the College Football Playoff conversation with an upset. away.blurb: The Gators started backup QB Tramell Jones Jr. in place of Aaron Philo, who was active but only available as the emergency QB. Jones and the Florida offense started slow. The Gators fell behind 17-3 into the second quarter, but a critical touchdown drive with less than a minute before halftime cut the margin to 17-10. Florida gives up punt return TD Florida went three-and-out on its first drive. Texas pulls together an 8-play, 60-yard drive that ends in a 38-yard field goal to extend the lead to 10-0 with 6:42 left in the first quarter. AUSTIN — Florida football has gotten back on track. The Gators defeated No. 6 Texas 27-24 Saturday at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, Texas, for their second top six win of the 2026 season. The victory snaps a two game losing streak for UF and is its first win since knocking off then-No. 6 Ole Miss on September 26. Jones and the Florida offense performed much better in the second half as UF totaled points on its first three drives to eventually lead 27-17. Arch Manning and Texas responded with a touchdown to make it 27-24, and after a Florida punt, UT held the chance to tie the game and take the lead. picks.headline: LSU vs. Mississippi State Final Score Predictions: Who Wins and Why?
picks.blurb: LSU vs. Mississippi State Final Score Predictions: Who Wins and Why? Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB After LSU traveled to Lexington last weekend, Lane Kiffin and the Tigers are coming off of a disappointing loss, heading into the Week 7 matchup against Mississippi State . LSU heads into the matchup with a recent loss, while the Bulldogs are also traveling to Baton Rouge after a loss to the Crimson Tide in Week 5. Before the No. 22 LSU Tigers host the No. 16 Mississippi State Bulldogs this Saturday, the LSU On SI team predicts which team will win and why. Oct 3, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers safety Tamarcus Cooley (0) intercepts a pass from McNeese Cowboys quarterback Jake Strong (not pictured) during the first half at Tiger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ross Abboud The time for sloppiness is over, and everyone in LSU’s football program knows it. Ole Miss was a game you could’ve won. Kentucky was a game you should never have lost. That will be LSU’s wake-up call. LSU 48, Mississippi State 24 Brooke Benedict Unlike last weekend's loss to Kentucky, LSU has to get both sides of the ball to play all four quarters, with the defense able to shut down Mississippi State's pass threat, and Sam Leavitt and his receiver options are able to make key plays during possessions. Without any system errors from the offense, defense and special teams, the team will see some much-needed success back at home, being able to win over the Bulldogs and win back their top-ranked reputation. LSU 33, Mississippi State 21 If Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor plays: Kamario Taylor has an incredible ability to control the long ball, which will force LSU's defense to account for that threat almost all of the time, and following the loss to Kentucky, I expect LSU to play a lot more tight man coverage. The LSU offense, clearly more comfortable playing at home, will establish the run with Dilin Jones against the MSST 3-3-5 defense, and LSU will win a close one late in the 4th. LSU 38, Mississippi State 31 If Taylor doesn't play: If Taylor is unavailable in Saturday's game, the MSST backup QB is not a clear answer. Redshirt Freshman Parker Puckett started in place of Taylor against Alabama, but SEC veteran AJ Swann is also a likely option to play. Regardless, I expect the Bulldogs will be less competitive without the SEC TD leader hurling the rock. LSU wins handily at home. LSU 44, Mississippi State 21 Mississippi State Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor (1) waits for the snap during the third quarter against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Adrian Ramirez Adrian Ramirez LSU will bounce back from its overtime loss to Kentucky with a strong performance at home in Tiger Stadium. If both Kamario Taylor and running back Fluff Bothwell miss or are limited by their injuries, I expect LSU’s defense to be too much for Mississippi State to handle. I think the Tigers come out with a point to prove and get to work proving it. LSU 31, Mississippi State 14 Hannah Garcia While there’s the possibility of Taylor and Bothwell being out for the game, the LSU defense is still missing key pieces in Spears and Whit Weeks. The receivers have struggled to find consistency all season with catching the ball and Sam Leavitt’s interception numbers are also something that I think could cause LSU to lose. Mississippi State 24, LSU 17 LSU is desperate to bounce back after a tough loss against Kentucky. The keys to this game are Kamario Taylor’s health and Mississippi State’s secondary. Taylor is one of college football’s best quarterbacks, and if he’s not healthy, LSU’s defensive game plan changes. Meanwhile, the Bulldogs allow the second-most passing yards per game in the SEC, so I expect Lane Kiffin to open up the playbook and attack that weakness. I think the Tigers handle business at home. LSU 35, Mississippi State 21 Published Oct 16, 2026 BROOKE BENEDICT Brooke Benedict is a sophomore at LSU, majoring in journalism. She is originally from Boulder, Colorado, and enjoys skiing, hiking, and Pilates. She's always enjoyed watching sports and the way sports bring people together. She has spent one semester as a sports columnist for the LSU student newspaper, and is am excited to continue her LSU sports reporting career with On SI. But Lane Kiffin's bunch lost to Ole Miss, came back with a few wins, and then last week got outfoxed by Kentucky in a 35-34 overtime loss. And now there's a problem. LSU is talented enough to beat anyone, but it's one more loss away from realistically being out of the College Football Playoff. That won't be easy with a brutal schedule over the second half of the season. Mississippi State has had two weeks to get over the 56-23 loss to Alabama. It isn't an easy slate, but at 4-1, it'll still be in the mix for big things if it can get out of Baton Rouge with a win. Mississippi State vs LSU: Quick Hits LSU starts a run of three home games in the next four weeks, going to Auburn next before hosting Alabama and Texas. Mississippi State starts its own run of four home games in five weeks after this, hosting Oklahoma before going to Texas. LSU has won three straight in the series ever since the 44-34 loss to open up the 2020 season. That came right after the Tigers' national title season. How To Watch Mississippi State vs LSU Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Tiger Stadium, Baton Rouge, LA – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Mississippi State Will Win The defense will have to step up its game. The Bulldogs have been winning on their amazing offense, but the defense has held its own in key spots. It might be tough to hang with the Tigers blow for blow, so taking the ball away is a must. Mississippi State came up with two takeaways in two of the last three games, and turnovers have been a big issue for LSU, with ten in six games. Why does the defense have to come up big? Why LSU Will Win Mississippi State might be without star quarterback Kamario Taylor. He's trying to get past a leg injury suffered in the Alabama loss, and now he and top running back Fluff Bothwell are questionable at best. There's also the home-field advantage side of this. Ole Miss and Kentucky are good, but LSU should've been better in both road games. At home, the Tigers have been untouchable, winning by a combined score of 194-44 in the four games. Mississippi State vs LSU Prediction, Betting Lines It'll be a different LSU team than the one that walked off the field against Kentucky. It'll be more confident, explosive, and it won't let up – this won't be a back-and-forth fight like it was against the Wildcats. Of course, this changes if Taylor is at 100% for the Bulldogs, but even if he's ready to roll, LSU will be razor-sharp with a much better defensive performance than last week. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:53 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 16 Mississippi State travels to No. 22 LSU for a massive SEC showdown. Can Lane Kiffin and the Tigers bounce back after an embarrassing loss? The pressure is mounting in Baton Rouge as No. 22 LSU (4-2) prepares to host No. 16 Mississippi State (4-2) Saturday afternoon at Tiger Stadium. Lane Kiffin's Tigers are coming off an embarrassing 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky, a game LSU had every opportunity to win before a questionable fourth-down decision allowed the Wildcats to force overtime. Meanwhile, Mississippi State is looking to bounce back after a disappointing loss to Alabama. With LSU already sitting at 1-2 in SEC play, another conference loss could effectively end the Tigers' College Football Playoff hopes. LSU: Can Sam Leavitt Save the Tigers? LSU's offense has shown flashes of brilliance under Kiffin, but consistency remains a major concern. Quarterback Sam Leavitt has thrown for 1,495 yards and 10 touchdowns, but his eight interceptions are the most of any quarterback in the SEC. Those turnovers have been a major issue for a team that possesses enough offensive talent to compete with nearly anyone. Running back Dilin Jones has provided stability in the backfield, rushing for 426 yards and five touchdowns through LSU's first five games. Wide receiver Winston Watkins Jr. has also emerged as a dangerous weapon, recording 354 receiving yards. Defensively, LSU has been impressive at times, particularly with edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, who recorded eight sacks through the team's first five games. However, the Tigers just surrendered 35 points to Kentucky, raising serious questions about their ability to close out games. Against Mississippi State's explosive offense, LSU cannot afford another inconsistent defensive performance. Mississippi State: Kamario Taylor Is a PROBLEM Jeff Lebby has Mississippi State playing some exciting football, and quarterback Kamario Taylor has emerged as one of the SEC's most dangerous young players. Taylor has thrown for 1,450 yards, 17 touchdowns, and just four interceptions while completing 66.2% of his passes. However, his availability is a major concern after aggravating a lower-leg injury against Alabama. If Taylor is healthy enough to play, LSU's defense will have its hands full. Wide receiver Anthony Evans III has been outstanding, recording 40 receptions for 574 yards and five touchdowns through five games. Running back Fluff Bothwell has also been productive, rushing for 403 yards and three touchdowns while averaging 5.4 yards per carry. The Bulldogs possess enough offensive firepower to challenge LSU, but their defense remains vulnerable. Mississippi State was allowing 28 points and nearly 380 yards per game through its first five contests. That's a dangerous weakness against a Kiffin-led offense playing at home. How Each Team Wins For LSU, everything starts with protecting the football. Leavitt must avoid costly interceptions and take advantage of Mississippi State's vulnerable secondary. Establishing Jones early should also create opportunities for explosive passing plays. Defensively, LSU needs to pressure Taylor if he plays and prevent Evans from creating big plays downfield. For Mississippi State, the formula revolves around attacking LSU's defense with tempo and forcing Leavitt into mistakes. If Taylor is available, his dual-threat ability could create serious problems. The Bulldogs must also establish Bothwell to prevent LSU from focusing entirely on the passing game. I expect an offensive shootout in Baton Rouge. Mississippi State has enough offensive talent to create problems for LSU, particularly if Taylor is healthy enough to play. However, I believe this is a bounce-back opportunity for Kiffin and the Tigers. Leavitt should have success attacking Mississippi State's secondary, and I expect him to throw for more than 300 yards and three touchdowns. The Bulldogs will keep things competitive throughout the afternoon, but LSU's home-field advantage and offensive firepower should ultimately make the difference. Expect Mississippi State to threaten late before LSU's defense comes up with a crucial stop to secure the victory. Final Score: No. 22 LSU 38, No. 16 Mississippi State 31 LSU survives a major scare, improves to 5-2, and keeps its College Football Playoff hopes alive. With the quarterback situation in flux due to Kamario Taylor's apparent turf toe injury sustained against Alabama, State enters the week as two touchdown underdogs on the first fall-like Saturday of football season. Coaches on both sides have a fair amount of familiarity with each other having worked together in Oxford from 2020-21 as boss and apprentice. If Lebby finds a way to get Taylor healthy and ready to roll on Saturday, this may be a barn burner inside Tiger Stadium based on the talent at the offensive skill positions for each team. Mississippi State enters the weeked ranked No. 16 nationally, according to the Week 7 AP Top 25 poll. With an extra week to lick its wounds and recover from a double-digit loss to Alabama, there's a possibility the Bulldogs can find a way to pull off a stunner and keep LSU out of the College Football Playoff entirely in Year 1 under Kiffin. The Bulldogs come in at No. 11 in the SEC, and No. 27 in ESPN's Football Power Index poll with a projected overall record of 8-4 following a 4-1 start on the season. WIth that familiarity, perhaps both coaches feel they understand each other well with tendencies in play calling. "They're really multiple. Zach [Arnett] was with us for a year [at Ole Miss]," Kiffin said Monday. "After Mississippi State, he came over. He's really smart. It's interesting, because he's running a little of his old defense and he's running (Pete) Golding's defense this year. Now, he's even more multiple." The numbers don't show a large discrepancy when it comes to winning and losing off of byes. "I think (open dates) are a little overrated that way. away.headline: Big names listed on LSU football vs. Mississippi State injury report
away.blurb: The first injury report for Mississippi State at LSU football dropped Wednesday night. It listed a handful of significant names. Most notably, Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor is questionable. Mississippi State RB Fluff Bothwell is also questionable. Bothwell is averaging over five yards per carry. The veteran back is a go-to option for Jeff Lebby's offense. Mississippi State linebacker Jalen Smith was listed as out, meaning the Bulldogs will be down a starter on defense. Mississippi State won't get much sympathy from an LSU team also dealing with the injury bug. LSU stars Trey'Dez Green and Whit Weeks remained sidelined and aren't expected back until November. Hybrid defensive back Da'Shawn Spears tore his ACL vs. Ole Miss and remains out for the year. LSU WR Phillip Wright and LB Charles Ross are also out for the year. Neither was a starter, but both saw rotational playing time and made impacts on special teams. Taylor left Mississippi State's Week 5 contest vs. Alabama (MSU was on bye in Week 6) with a lower-body injury. Earlier this week, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported Taylor's status was in flux. The betting spread has moved in LSU's favor since the opening line, indicating bettors think Taylor may not play. Taylor, one of the country's best quarterbacks, would be a significant loss for Mississippi State. The offense runs through Taylor, and the dynamic QB was generating Heisman buzz earlier this year. LSU vs. Mississippi State is set for this Saturday at 11 AM in Tiger Stadium. away.headline: LSU football injury report | Who made the list ahead of Mississippi State game?
away.blurb: Sophomore linebacker Tylen Singleton was listed as questionable on the first SEC-mandated injury report of the week for No. 21 LSU's (4-2, 1-2 SEC) game against the Bulldogs that was released Wednesday night. BATON ROUGE — An already depleted position group for the LSU football team might be down another member when it takes the field against Mississippi State on Saturday, Oct. 17. This is the first time Singleton has found his way onto an injured list for the Tigers this season. And it comes at a less than ideal time as quarterback Kamario Taylor and the high-flying No. 19 Mississippi State (4-1, 2-1) offense comes to Baton Rouge for a pivotal conference showdown. EVALUATING LSU THROUGH SIX GAMES Grading Lane Kiffin, LSU football at the season midpoint LSU RANKINGS Where is LSU football ranked after overtime loss at Kentucky in Week 6? LSU is already down star senior linebacker Whit Weeks, who fractured the fibula in his right leg against Texas A&M on Sept. 26. So LSU defensive coordinator Blake Baker was already calling on a reserve to step into a more prevalent role within the defense. Reserve linebacker Charles Ross II also suffered a lower leg injury against McNeese on Oct. 3. Singleton has earned more snaps since Weeks' injury. Through six games, he has eight tackles. As expected, LSU will be without star junior tight end Trey'Dez Green, safety Dashawn Spears and sophomore wide receiver Phillip Wright III against Mississippi State on Saturday. away.headline: Scott Rabalais: Much was strange about LSU-Mississippi State, but Tigers get big win they needed
away.blurb: Mississippi State was ranked higher (16th) than LSU (22nd), but the entire thing felt like a fait accompli once word was passed that dangerous Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor and their talented running back Fluff Bothwell were both out with injuries. State was forced to start redshirt freshman Parker Puckett at quarterback, a player with only 14 career pass attempts, which happens to be 14 more than you or I have in an SEC game. To a college football world outside Louisiana (and some in it) that is rooting for LSU and Lane Kiffin to go careening out of the College Football Playoff picture three weeks before the first CFP rankings are released, it seemed like a bully bad break for State. Yes, it took something off LSU’s conquest that arguably the Bulldogs’ two best players were out. But there was nothing Kiffin’s Tigers could do about that. You play who is playing, period. And State didn’t hold back anything just because LSU was without guys like Trey’Dez Green on offense and Whit Weeks on defense. home.headline: LSU recruit Peyton Houston nabs postive report from doctors on injury
home.blurb: LSU commitment Peyton “Pop” Houston of Evangel could return to running the Eagles’ offense before the regular season ends after visits with doctors on Monday. That’s good news for Eagles fans who saw the 4-star recruit be sidelined with a shoulder injury in the second quarter of the Eagles’ Oct. 16 home football game against Cornerstone Christian out of Texas. Evangel had jumped out to a 10-0 lead against Cornerstone and trailed just 14-10 at halftime. But the visitors (6-2) exploded in the second half without facing Houston and left Rodney Duron Field with a 49-23 victory. “Peyton received a great report following MRI and X-Ray scans,” said Shaun Houston, his father. “He has a grade 2 AC joint sprain that had no ligament tears, bone breaks nor fractures. With rehab and rest, he should be back in a couple of weeks.” Two doctors on the Eagles’ sideline looked at Houston but he was not transported to a hospital. Instead, he remained on the sideline with ice on his shoulder, cheering for his team. In Houston’s place, Briggs Berlin, the son of former Evangel great Brock Berlin, took over the team and tossed a pair of TD passes. “Briggs did fine and he’ll continue to do so until we see how the situation with Pop develops,” Duron said. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Georgia Football's Clash with Auburn on Saturday
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Georgia Football's Clash with Auburn on Saturday Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Georgia Bulldogs will face off against the Auburn Tigers in the Deep South’s Oldest Rivalry on Saturday afternoon. The weather forecast calls for a beautiful fall Saturday, where the high in Athens is supposed to be just 67 degrees. The betting forecast is calling for the Dawgs to beat the Tigers by about three touchdowns. This will likely not be a close game, which means we can be a little looser with our bold predictions for it. Here are three bold ones for Kirby Smart and Alex Golesh’s first game in this rivalry: Georgia has a 100-Yard Rusher and Receiver The Dawgs can take advantage of this Auburn defense, which is a bottom half unit in the conference, allowing over 350 yards of total offense per game. Georgia’s offense has been extremely productive, ranking top three in the conference. Georgia having a back and a wideout go for 100 yards in the same game hasn’t happened in 10 years. So, yeah. This is a bold prediction. I think about a guy like Talyn Taylor or Craig Dandridge, who have hit on some explosive passing plays. All it takes is one or two of those and some screens and underneath throws to work for that 100-yard game to come into play. Auburn is also among the worst rushing defenses in the SEC. We saw Dwight Phillips Jr. run for over 100 yards against Alabama on just 17 carries. He, Nate Frazier and Bo Walker have each registered multiple explosive runs. All it takes is for one of them to bust a huge run and that 100-yard mark is well within reach. Dawgs go for 250 On the Ground Auburn is allowing about 150 yards per game on the ground. I think Georgia could go for over 250. They have done it twice already and ran for over 200 yards in two other games. Auburn allowed almost 250 yards to both Tennessee and Florida. Georgia has a better offense than both of those teams. The Dawgs could really blow Auburn out on Saturday, and if they do that then there will be a lot of yards gained on the ground. Partially due to garbage time. Georgia Holds Auburn to Under 300 Total Yards Auburn has possibly the most unique offense that Georgia will see all year. There is an argument to be made that the Dawgs will struggle more in this game than you would initially think because of that. Auburn takes the least amount of time in between plays and runs more options and designed quarterback run plays than any other offense that Georgia will see this year. I am not buying it. Georgia’s defense has been the best in college football. The Dawgs will shut down Auburn on Saturday. After dominating Alabama physically, the Bulldogs could embarrass the Tigers. The Deep South's Oldest Rivalry returns to Athens this Saturday as No. 1 Georgia (6-0) welcomes Auburn (3-2) to Sanford Stadium for a 3:30 p.m. ET showdown on ESPN. And this matchup could get ugly quickly. Kirby Smart's Bulldogs are coming off an impressive 20-17 road victory over Alabama, while Auburn suffered a disappointing 24-14 loss at Tennessee. Georgia has also won nine consecutive meetings against Auburn, including last year's 20-10 victory in Jordan-Hare Stadium. Georgia: The Bulldogs Are Built DIFFERENT Georgia might have delivered its most impressive performance of the season against Alabama. Despite missing its top two running backs, Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens, the Bulldogs rushed for 206 yards against one of the SEC's most talented defenses. Dwight Phillips Jr. stepped up in a major way, while Bo Walker provided additional production in the backfield. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was outstanding, completing 18 of 22 passes for 249 yards while accounting for two touchdowns. Through six games, Stockton has thrown for 1,298 yards and 14 touchdowns, completing more than 76% of his passes. Defensively, Georgia held Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell to just 185 passing yards while recording four sacks. With Chris Cole, Raylen Wilson, KJ Bolden, and Ellis Robinson IV leading the defense, Georgia has the personnel to completely overwhelm Auburn's offense. Auburn: Can the Tigers Even Keep This Competitive? Auburn enters Saturday with serious questions surrounding its offense. Quarterback Byrum Brown has thrown for approximately 1,055 yards with seven touchdowns and seven interceptions. While he's dangerous with his legs, his decision-making has been inconsistent. Against Tennessee, Brown rushed for 107 yards but threw two interceptions in the 24-14 loss. Wide receiver Keshaun Singleton has emerged as a reliable target, recording 29 receptions for 322 yards. However, Auburn's biggest concern might be its inability to consistently stop the run. Tennessee rushed for 237 yards against the Tigers last weekend. That's a terrible sign considering Georgia just rushed for more than 200 yards against Alabama without its top two backs. If Auburn can't contain Georgia's rushing attack, this game could be over by halftime. How Each Team Wins For Georgia, the formula is simple: establish the running game, control the line of scrimmage, and force Brown to beat its defense through the air. Stockton should have plenty of opportunities to attack Auburn's secondary once the Tigers begin loading the box. Defensively, Georgia must contain Brown's mobility and force him into obvious passing situations. For Auburn, everything starts with avoiding turnovers and creating explosive plays. Brown must use his legs to extend drives, while the Tigers' defense needs to generate pressure on Stockton. Auburn cannot afford to fall behind early and become one-dimensional. I don't see this game being particularly competitive. Georgia is coming off an emotional victory over Alabama, but Kirby Smart has built a program that rarely overlooks inferior opponents, especially rivals. The Bulldogs should dominate the line of scrimmage, and I expect another massive rushing performance regardless of whether Frazier and Bowens return. Stockton should have an efficient afternoon, throwing multiple touchdowns while Georgia's defense forces Brown into at least two turnovers. Expect the Bulldogs to establish a commanding lead before halftime and eventually begin rotating younger players into the game. Final Score: No. 1 Georgia 41, Auburn 10 Georgia dominates its oldest rival, improves to 7-0, and continues looking like the team to beat in college football. No, it's not nearly as fierce as the Iron Bowl when Alabama takes on Auburn, but when you've played 130 times, you tend to have a few interesting moments that build into something generational. Georgia just got by Alabama in a controversial 20-17 thriller – let's just say the Bulldogs got a wee bit of a break on a key Crimson Tide deep shot – and now it's the No. 1 team in the country. Auburn has had two weeks off to get ready for this, and knocking the Bulldogs off of their lofty perch would put the first season under head coach Alex Golesh into hyperdrive. Auburn vs Georgia: Quick Hits Auburn gets LSU and the Lane Kiffin show next, and then goes to Ole Miss. Georgia gets a week off before playing the Cocktail Party showdown against Florida in Atlanta, and then it goes to Ole Miss. Georgia has won seven times in the series since losing in 2017 (it was No. 1 in the nation then, too), but it won the SEC Championship a few weeks later. The Bulldogs have won 11 of the last 12 meetings. It might have been hit hard by Florida, but it does a lot of bending without breaking, thanks to plenty of sacks, lots of plays behind the line, and a third down defense that's holding up well. Offensively, the high-tempo Tiger attack should be able to keep the Bulldogs on their heels. Alabama ran well last week, but it only handed the ball off 29 times. Auburn won't make that mistake, pushing for at least 35 carries, and close to 40, as it tries to hit the Georgia defense with tempo. Why Georgia Will Win Georgia's defensive front will live in the Auburn backfield. It's a problem with Auburn's style that it allows defenses to tee off on the quarterback and come up with too many tackles for loss. The Tigers don't worry about the time of possession battle, and they're good at overcoming negative plays with something positive, but Georgia has the defense to swarm all over the quick-hitting short plays. Auburn doesn't do anything deep, and Georgia should limit any yards after the catch or runs that get to the second level. Auburn vs Georgia Prediction, Betting Lines It's been an interesting start to the Golesh era. The offense is supposed to dominate and take over, but it doesn't do it enough. The defense that was so great last year has stayed strong, but it's about to get pounded on. Auburn's two losses came when it allowed over three yards per carry. Georgia is averaging over six yards per pop. The Georgia Bulldogs are the No. 1 team in the country. Auburn is a team that's trying to turn their program around. And, Alex Golesh is looking for that first unranked-upset win over a rival. Can he get it done on Saturday? A to Z Sports' experts picked the final scores for this game. Final score predictions for Georgia vs. Auburn Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama : Georgia 30 Auburn 10 After watching the Georgia Bulldogs run all over the SEC's top-ranked rushing defense in Tuscaloosa, Auburn may be in trouble. Truthfully, Georgia is the best team in the country, and Auburn is rebuilding under first-year head coach Alex Golesh. I don't think this team has the explosiveness to score on Georgia, and they certainly don't have the physicality to win the trench battle on either side. Gunner Srockton has also elevated his game this season, making multiple high-leverage throws against Alabama in an extremely tough environment. The Dawgs will roll in this one. Tyler Forness, A to Z Florida : Georgia 45, Auburn 17 I don't see this as much of a game. The Bulldogs are coming off a big win over the Alabama Crimson Tide and showed they can hang with the best in the business. This Auburn Tigers team is in good hands with Alex Golesh, but they aren't there yet. Byrum Brown won't be able to generate much against another great Bulldogs defense. This one will likely be over at halftime. Ryan Roberts, A to Z Notre Dame : Georgia 38, Auburn 14 Georgia looks like the most complete team in the country right now, and I don't see Auburn keeping up for long in this matchup. The Bulldogs have the talent, physicality, and balance to control both sides of the ball, and I expect them to establish dominance early. Gunner Stockton is poised for a big game, taking advantage of Auburn's defense and helping Georgia put points on the board consistently. Once the Bulldogs find their offensive rhythm, the Tigers could struggle to keep this one competitive. The Georgia defense could be just as impressive. Auburn will likely have a few moments, but I don't expect the Tigers to sustain enough offense to seriously threaten the Bulldogs. Georgia can generate pressure, force mistakes, and turn defensive stops into scoring opportunities, letting the lead grow as the game progresses. This matchup highlights just how dangerous Georgia can be when all three phases click. The Bulldogs pull away comfortably and send another message to the country. Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee : Georgia 44, Auburn 20 Boy, we've kind of forgotten about Gunner Stockton in the big picture, haven't we? The Dawgs' starting quarterback has gotten lost in the shuffle this year, with strong quarterback play from Darian Mensah, Keelon Russell, Kamario Taylor, Josh Hoover, and others. But make no mistake, he executes his team's offense as well as any signal caller in the country, as we saw in Georgia's 20-17 win over Alabama last weekend. More of the same will come on Saturday against an Auburn team that will fight for a half and then find itself out of this by the third quarter. Stockton will continue to impress, running when he needs to and spreading the ball around at a high percentage (18/22 passing last week, with completions by 10 different pass catchers). Georgia might be banged up at RB, but Dwight Phillips Jr.'s 120 yards last week against Bama proved they're basically plug-and-play in the backfield. Justin Churchill, A to Z Oklahoma : Georgia 30, Auburn 10 The Georgia Bulldogs have now proven they are the No. 1 team in the country. Their win over Alabama is about as good as it gets for any team this season, other than maybe Texas beating Ohio State. But, they have to show they can be consistent. And, there are definitely still things to work on. As for Auburn, this offense has not been as fun to watch as we all maybe thought it would in the offseason. But Georgia has the mix of defense and offense that Auburn just simply won't be able to hang around with. Then again, this is a rivalry game, and we've seen some weird things happen in rivalry games this year alone. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. The Crimson Tide will be looking to avoid losing consecutive regular season games for the first time since 2007, while the Volunteers will be seeking to snap a four-game home losing streak against ranked opponents. Alabama (5-1, 3-1 SEC) took a 20-17 home loss to Georgia last week, which leaves the Crimson Tide with a dwindling margin for error entering the second half of their schedule. Tennessee (5-1, 2-1) is coming off an ugly 24-17 win at Arkansas in need of the resume boost that would come with knocking off Alabama. While Tennessee's defense is thriving midway through the season, facing Alabama will be its toughest test yet. Though Alabama star receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams is expected to miss the game due to injury, Bama's offense will still pack a punch that tests Tennessee's secondary. The Volunteers counter with the nation's No. 15 rushing offense and a languishing passing attack that will need to get better if they are going to pull an upset that would reverberate through the SEC and beyond. With blowout road wins over quality foes Kentucky and Mississippi State already in hand, the Tide will look to keep rolling on the road with their first win in Knoxville since 2020. But something will have to give as the Crimson Tide have dropped two straight inside Neyland Stadium. Whichever team is smoking, the traditional postgame victory cigars will hit a little different this time. Tennessee's QB question: Tennessee sophomore quarterback George MacIntyre made his first career start last week in the Volunteers' 24-17 win at Arkansas, stepping in for injured and underperforming freshman Faizon Brandon . Now the question is how long the Volunteers will stick with MacIntyre, who completed 18 of 29 passes for 247 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions against the Razorbacks. Regardless of who gets the nod against Alabama, the Crimson Tide's priority will be to slow down the SEC's second-leading rusher, DeSean Bishop , and to make Tennessee's fledgling passing attack prove that it can deliver. Playoff implications: With a win, Alabama will have an 87.7% chance of reaching the College Football Playoff, according to the CBS Sports College Football Playoff Forecaster. Because the Crimson Tide won't respect the Volunteers' passing game, they'll be able to load the box and frustrate Tennessee's ground game, much like Texas did in Week 4. My Alabama vs. Tennessee predictions for today's game from Neyland Stadium (3:30 p.m. ET, ABC) have the Crimson Tide rolling to a win as 7.5-point road favorites. My college football picks are also calling for a high-scoring SEC tilt on Saturday, Oct. 17. TOP PICK Who will win Alabama vs Tennessee: Alabama -7.5 If last week was any indicator, Tennessee has far more problems than Alabama , despite the Volunteers' win and the Crimson Tide's loss. In George MacIntyre's first start for Josh Heupel, he finished with just a 10.3 QBR in a seven-point win against Arkansas. He'll be starting again against Bama, which is why I like the Tide to cover -9.5 or better . Arkansas lost to its previous three Power Four opponents by an average of 29.3 points, including a 28-point defeat to Georgia — the same team Alabama lost to by just three on the road last week. Tennessee's offense won't be able to keep up with Alabama. Keelon Russell ranks third nationally in QBR (90.0) , and the Tide are top 20 in offensive success rate (50.1%). The Alabama vs. Tennessee rivalry history is full of winning streaks, and this could be the start of another. Alabama vs Tennessee Over/Under pick: Over 50.5 For this Over to hit (I'd take it at 51.5 or better ), Alabama will need to do the bulk of the scoring, and the Tide will push for 31+ points given Russell's recent play. The former five-star recruit has put up an 8 0.9+ QBR in four straight games while accounting for 14 TDs. His dual-threat ability has helped open up the run game, too, with Alabama ranking fourth nationally in rush success rate (53.3%) . That will force Jim Knowles' defense to stay honest instead of solely focusing on protecting the back end. Meanwhile, Tennessee should be able to put up 20+ points to help push the total Over. The Volunteers have one of the best run games in the country (No. 2 in EPA per rush), led by DeSean Bishop . Bishop ranks top 10 nationally in rushing yards after contact (465). Alabama vs Tennessee prop: Alabama team total Over 29.5 Given how loaded Alabama's offense is, I like the Over at 30.5 or better , especially with how the Tide matchup against Tennessee's defense. Even with Ryan Coleman-Williams out, Alabama remains loaded at the skill positions, with eight other players topping 180 yards from scrimmage this season. That includes Lotzeir Brooks , who leads the Tide in yards per route run (2.76). Russell, Brooks, and Co. should take advantage of a Volunteers defense that's 70th nationally in pass success rate (43.9%). Alabama rarely squanders opportunities either, ranking third in the country in points per opportunity (5.27) . Alabama vs Tennessee combo One word describes Tennessee's passing game: rocky. The Volunteers are 128th nationally in pass success rate (33.8) , and MacIntyre has a QBR of 24.7 this season. That won't cut it against an Alabama defense tied for the 14th-most sacks in the country (17). I'm expecting a fast start from Russell after last week's tough loss to Georgia, and once Bama takes the lead, Tennessee isn't equipped to come back with MacIntyre behind center. The Tide, who are ninth nationally on defense in rush success rate (35.4%), should be able to focus on slowing Bishop enough to win by 10+ points.
