Best Alabama vs Tennessee props Prop pick #1: Keelon Russell Over 240.5 Pass Yards (53.27%) Alabama star sophomore quarterback Keelon Russell should be amped up to bounce back after an underwhelming 16-for-30, 185-yard performance with just one touchdown in the Crimson Tide's loss to Georgia. That said, it came against arguably the best defense in the country. It was Russell's worst performance since throwing for just 188 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in Week 2 against Kentucky. Over six games this season, Russell still averages more than this prop at 266.5 passing yards per game. He draws a Tennessee defense that has shut down quarterbacks all season, allowing just 185 passing yards per game. However, what elite quarterback have the Volunteers actually shut down? "Well, they held Arch Manning to just 201 yards." Oh, like that holds up in the year of our Lord 2026. Russell is far better than Manning and has faced far tougher competition this season than what this Volunteers pass defense has seen. Coming off a matchup against one of the country's best defenses, the sophomore should clear 240 passing yards on Saturday. Take this up to 250.5 passing yards. Prop pick #2: DeSean Bishop Over 89.5 Rush Yards (50.74%) With Tennessee's run-heavy offense averaging nearly 43 rushing attempts per game this season, I don't expect that approach to change on Saturday against a very talented Alabama run defense. Over their last three games against Texas, Auburn, and Arkansas, the Volunteers still average 38.33 attempts per game . Tennessee should lean on its leading rusher, DeSean Bishop , to move the ball downfield . Last week against Georgia, this Crimson Tide defense showed some flaws when junior running back Dwight Phillips Jr. rushed for 120 yards on just 17 carries . That's the same number of carries Bishop averages per game this season, and Alabama is coming off a game where it struggled to stop the run. Bishop is averaging 113 yards per game and more than six yards per carry this season. If he gets his usual workload, he should be in a great spot to record 90-plus rushing yards on Saturday. Take this up to 95+ yards. Prop pick #3: Keelon Russell Over 24.5 Rush Yards (53.49%) I gave out this same prop last week, so I'll start this one the same way: If you can secure Russell's longest rush over 15.5 yards , take it! Russell has surpassed that mark in every game this season. Plus, the longest rush prop eliminates the possibility of sacks taking away rushing yards, so if you can access it, take it Over his standard rushing yards prop at 25+. However, Russell has still rushed for Over 25 yards in four of his six games this season . The sophomore quarterback is averaging 7.66 rushing attempts per game, and with the Crimson Tide likely to be leading, as the spread indicates, they'll eventually want to chew some clock. That should give Russell plenty of chances to rack up yards on the ground. The last mobile quarterback Tennessee faced was Auburn's Byrum Brown, who averages 16.2 rushing attempts per game and racked up more than 107 rushing yards against the Volunteers. Russell just needs 25 and should have plenty of opportunities on Saturday. Take this up to 30+ rushing yards. away.headline: What Zabien Brown injury means for Alabama football defense
away.blurb: "A lot of these guys are kind of in the same boat," coach Kalen DeBoer said. ... "Zabien, lower leg injury, you know, trying to evaluate throughout the week what he looks like." Brown left Alabama's 26-10 loss to Tennessee Saturday, Oct. 17 at Neyland Stadium in the second quarter after recording two tackles. Brown returned to the sideline at halftime in his jersey over a hoodie with sweatpants on. "Both of them, both Zabien and EJ, have lower extremity injuries, and we will work through it here later this week," DeBoer said postgame Saturday. "I don't have much more than that." What Zabien Brown injury means for Alabama football DB room For three seasons Brown has been a staple of Alabama's defensive backfield. In 2026, he's tied with Yhonzae Pierre for the team-lead with four pass deflections. Brown has one of six Alabama fumble recoveries. And, per Pro Football Focus, Brown has allowed 12 receptions on 22 targets for 207 yards and one touchdown. Alabama may now have to turn to Dijon Lee Jr., who has struggled at times in 2026, and Mercer transfer Carmelo O'Neal in Brown's absence. Lee had three tackles including one for loss against Tennessee, while O'Neal had three tackles in a season-high 62 snaps, per PFF. Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS Somewhat quietly, one of the bigger games on college football slate this weekend is happening at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium between No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) and No. 13 Missouri (5-1, 2-1 SEC). Both squads enter with one loss and need a win this weekend to maintain a reasonable path to the College Football Playoffs. However, alongside the high-stakes of the matchup are the storylines revolving around each team’s roster. Rebels’ star running back Kewan Lacy will be facing his former team for the first time since leaving Missouri, following his true freshman season in 2024. Meanwhile, former Ole Miss starters Austin Simmons, Cayden Lee and Chris Graves Jr. all return to Oxford for the first time since they entered the transfer portal, following the Rebels’ deep run through last year’s playoffs. Saturday’s kickoff between the Rebels and Tigers is set for 2:30 p.m. CT on the SEC Network. Ole Miss entered the week as six-point home favorites. Ahead of the Rebels' latest pressure-filled matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Sep 26, 2026; Gainesville, Florida, USA; Mississippi Rebels head coach Pete Golding looks on after an interception against the Florida Gators during the second half at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis Welcome to the gauntlet that is the College Football Playoffs….or at least the very real warmup version of it. The loser of this weekend’s game in Oxford isn’t mathematically out of the 12-team race, but it’s going to be a loss that will be immensely hard to overcome looking at Ole Miss’ and Missouri’s schedule. As far as the actual matchup is concerned, going into the game, Missouri has played better on the defensive side of the ball and matches the Rebels’ offensive firepower with Austin Simmons and Jamal Roberts leading the way. The Tigers’ rush attack could have the ability to give the Rebels a long afternoon, and we’ll really find out if Ole Miss improved enough from its nightmare performance defending the run against Florida. Ole Miss doesn’t have to completely shut down Mizzou’s ground game, it more than likely won’t, but if it can limit Roberts and the rest of the production in the backfield, the Rebels should give themselves a real chance at picking up a critical win. In my mind, that’s going to be the key to victory for Ole Miss. I believe this game will come down to the final few possessions and whichever offense has the ball last in that scenario. Given the large sample size we’ve seen of Trinidad Chambliss in those types of situations, I have a hard time picking against those results. Ole Miss 34, Missouri 31 Matt Galatzan All of the talk is going to be about the return of Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee to Oxford, and Kewan Lacy facing off against his former team. However, there needs to be more talk about Missouri's defense, or more specifically, its pass rush. The Tigers have 18 sacks this year, which is tied with Texas for third in the SEC behind LSU and Tennessee. Meanwhile, the Rebels are No. 1 in the SEC in sacks allowed with just five. If the Rebels can protect Trinidad Chambliss and slow down a balanced Missouri offense, they will be in good shape. I think they do both just enough to get the win. Ole Miss 30, Missouri 27 I think Ole Miss will take home a hard-fought victory against former Rebels’ quarterback Austin Simmons, wide receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. and the rest of the Missouri Tigers. Simmons, Lee and running back Jamal Roberts are likely to give head coach Pete Golding and his defense trouble, leading to a “bend-don’t-break” type of performance, following a bounce-back game against Vanderbilt for the Rebels’ defense. However, I’m comfortable predicting Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, wide receiver Deuce Alexander and running back Kewan Lacy to outplay Simmons, Lee and Roberts and give the Rebels a high-scoring ranked win in Ole Miss’ homecoming game. Ole Miss 38, Missouri 31 Zion Trammell Ole Miss and Missouri feature star-studded quarterbacks in Trinidad Chambliss and Austin Simmons. This has the makings of a high-scoring affair, so whichever quarterback can protect the ball better could decide the outcome. I think Chambliss and Kewan Lacy play their best games of the year, and Ole Miss gets by with a win. Ole Miss 31, Missouri 28 Cooper Ferguson Back in the Vaught, I want to see a great response to the blowout victory in Nashville. All will go well if Trinidad Chambliss plays as he has so far. After a second-half respite in the Vanderbilt game, Kewan Lacy is primed for a breakout game in the 2026 campaign. I fear the talent and connection between Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee, but I do not see the Rebels dropping a game at VHS this season. Published Oct 16, 2026 TYLER KOMIS Bio: Tyler Komis is a beat reporter for Ole Miss On SI. He is a Biletnikoff Award and Lombardi Award voter from New Jersey with more than five years of sports reporting experience. Prior to joining On SI, he previously covered Ole Miss Athletics for 247Sports (2021-2026), chronicling the ascension of the football program and the beginning of its coaching transition to Pete Golding ahead of the 2025-26 College Football Playoffs. You can find Komis on social media channels, including X/Twitter @TylerKomis. picks.headline: Rece Davis Predicts Missouri-Ole Miss Winner After Changing His Pick on Air
picks.blurb: Rece Davis Predicts Missouri-Ole Miss Winner After Changing His Pick on Air Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Rece Davis expected to be the only voice backing No. 13 Missouri at No. 9 Ole Miss on Saturday, but the College GameDay host changed his prediction after ESPN’s Dan Wetzel and Pete Thamel both took the Tigers first. Davis made his pick on the College GameDay Podcast . He’s forecasting a back-and-forth game in Oxford that ends with the Rebels holding off former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons and the Tigers. Why Rece Davis switched his pick Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) hands the ball off to running back Makhi Frazier (25) against the Vanderbilt Commodores | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis came into the segment leaning toward Missouri (5-1, 2-1 SEC). That’s the same side ESPN analyst Greg McElroy took earlier this week . Davis came into the segment leaning toward Missouri (5-1, 2-1 SEC). That’s the same side ESPN analyst Greg McElroy took earlier this week . “You guys have surprised me because I thought for sure I was going to be the only one to pick Missouri,” Davis said. “I’m going to change my mind a little bit. Not just because you guys took Missouri, but I was leaning Missouri. Austin Simmons’ revenge, running game, the whole thing.” Davis also pointed to Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz, saying “a lot of times when Drink hits the mic, sometimes it doesn’t work out as well for the Tigers.” His forecast echoes Sept. 26, when Missouri gave up a fourth-quarter lead in a 31-24 loss at Mississippi State. “A back-and-forth game, up and down. Probably ends up much like Missouri’s last trip to the state of Mississippi,” Davis said. “I’ll say the Rebels hang on. I’ll be the one who says the home team wins it.” Missouri’s top-10 history at stake Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz reacts toward a referee during the first quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Missouri has rolled since that loss. The Tigers routed No. 8 Florida 45-17 , giving Drinkwitz his first regular-season win over a top-10 team in 11 tries at Missouri, and then beat Texas A&M 27-6. Missouri has rolled since that loss. The Tigers routed No. 8 Florida 45-17 , giving Drinkwitz his first regular-season win over a top-10 team in 11 tries at Missouri, and then beat Texas A&M 27-6. “If Missouri can do it, having a top-10 win because the Gators were top 10 at the time, they can win multiple games against top-10 teams for the first time since 1978,” Davis said. That 1978 team shut out defending national champion Notre Dame 3-0 and beat No. 2 Nebraska 35-31. Simmons lost Ole Miss’ starting job after a Week 2 ankle injury against Kentucky in 2025. At Missouri, the left-hander has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns and one interception, which is one yard fewer than Trinidad Chambliss has for the Rebels. Tigers running back Jamal Roberts leads the SEC in rushing. He’ll face an Ole Miss run defense that ranks last in the conference at 176.4 yards allowed per game and 106th nationally in EPA per rush allowed . “The Ole Miss defense hasn’t been what we thought it was going to be,” Davis said. “I remember talking to some people in the preseason, thinking this might be one of the best defensive fronts in college football. Maybe it’ll turn out to be, but so far we haven’t seen evidence of that.” How can Ole Miss hang on? Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) counters with Chambliss, a Heisman Trophy contender who’s back for another season after he won an injunction against the NCAA , and running back Kewan Lacy, who began his career at Missouri. “There’s also a little bit at stake here in the personal rivalry for Trinidad Chambliss, too. Maybe Kewan Lacy,” Davis said. Lacy set Ole Miss’ single-season record with 1,567 rushing yards in 2025 and signed a deal to return to Oxford . Still, his health hangs over this week. A shoulder injury kept him out of the 52-28 loss at Florida, and he left last week’s 52-17 win at Vanderbilt after seven carries. The Rebels’ offense ranks eighth nationally in success rate, while Missouri’s defense has allowed 23 points total across its last two games. Kickoff is 3:30 p.m. ET on SEC Network, and the loser falls to 2-2 in SEC play. Traders should not disregard Missouri's early-season road struggles. Home-field advantage and a little extra motivation to end a historic losing streak could be deciding factors in Ole Miss successfully covering. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:27 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 13 Missouri travels to No. 9 Ole Miss for a massive SEC showdown. Can the Tigers pull off another upset, or will the Rebels defend Oxford? Two of the SEC's most intriguing teams are set to collide Saturday afternoon as No. 13 Missouri (5-1) travels to Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1). Both programs are coming off dominant victories. Missouri dismantled Texas A&M 27-6, while Ole Miss embarrassed Vanderbilt 52-17. With both teams sitting at 2-1 in conference play, Saturday's matchup could have major implications for the SEC Championship race and College Football Playoff. Missouri: The Tigers Are Legitimate Contenders Eli Drinkwitz has Missouri playing some outstanding football, particularly on defense. The Tigers are allowing just 17.7 points per game and rank eighth nationally in rushing defense, surrendering approximately 78 yards per contest. Offensively, former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns, and just one interception. Now, he gets an opportunity to prove himself against his former program. But Missouri's biggest weapon has been running back Jamal Roberts. Roberts has rushed for 828 yards and eight touchdowns, including consecutive 200-yard performances. Against an Ole Miss defense allowing 176.4 rushing yards per game, he could be in for another massive afternoon. Former Ole Miss wide receiver Cayden Lee has also been outstanding, recording 42 receptions for 616 yards and five touchdowns. If Missouri establishes its rushing attack early, the Tigers could control this game. Ole Miss: Can Trinidad Chambliss Carry the Rebels? Pete Golding has Ole Miss back in the national conversation following last season's historic playoff run. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss continues to be one of the most exciting players in college football, throwing for 1,435 yards and 11 touchdowns through five games. Wide receiver Deuce Alexander has emerged as his favorite target, recording 32 receptions for 503 yards and five touchdowns. The Rebels are averaging 38.8 points and nearly 434 yards per game, but their defense remains a major concern. Ole Miss is allowing 28 points per game, including an embarrassing 52-point performance against Florida earlier this season. And facing Missouri's balanced offense certainly won't make things easier. However, the Rebels have been outstanding at home, winning all three of their games in Oxford this season. How Each Team Wins Missouri must establish Roberts early and force Ole Miss into a physical, defensive battle. If the Tigers can dominate time of possession and limit explosive plays from Chambliss, they have an excellent opportunity to leave Oxford with a victory. For Ole Miss, everything starts with its passing attack. Missouri's defense has been elite against the run, meaning Chambliss will likely need to carry the offense. The Rebels must also force Simmons into mistakes and prevent Roberts from consistently reaching the second level. This matchup has all the ingredients for one of the best SEC games of the weekend. Missouri's rushing attack should give the Rebels serious problems, and I expect Roberts to surpass 100 yards once again. However, I trust Chambliss and the Ole Miss offense to deliver when it matters most. The Rebels' explosive passing attack, combined with a sold-out Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, should be enough to overcome Missouri's physicality. Expect a back-and-forth contest that comes down to the final minutes, with Chambliss engineering a late scoring drive to secure the victory. The Tigers are 5-1, and the Rebels are 4-1, but each of their losses was in conference play, meaning the loser of this is all but out of the SEC title chase. Ole Miss got back up off the mat after a 52-28 loss to Florida with a week off and a 52-17 annihilation of Vanderbilt. With a rough back half of the season coming up, it can't give away this home game. Mizzou keeps on rolling, following up its 45-17 destruction of Florida with a strong 27-6 win over Texas A&M. But now it has to deal with a road game – it lost to Mississippi State the first time it had to leave CoMo in conference play. Missouri vs Ole Miss: Quick Hits Ole Miss needs this win with a trip to Texas up next, and Georgia and at Oklahoma coming after a home game against Auburn. Missouri is starting a run of three road games in the next four, going to Arkansas next, before hosting Texas and then going to Georgia. The two teams haven't played since 2019, a 38-27 Missouri win. The Tigers are 7-1 all-time in the series, with Ole Miss only winning the 1974 opener 10-0. It stuffed Jadan Baugh and Florida, holding the Gators to just 42 yards on the ground, and followed it up by turning into a brick wall against the Texas A&M attack, allowing just 27 yards on 23 carries. It's not like they're doing anything that special. They're getting behind the line, doing a great job of not allowing anything up the middle, and they should have success against an Ole Miss running game that's fine – even with Kewan Lacy back – but hardly dominant. Why Ole Miss Will Win Missouri has only faced one quarterback and passing game that can really rock – Kamario Taylor and Mississippi State – and it lost. Give credit to the Tigers for holding up against Florida, Texas A&M, and Kansas – they can actually throw a little – but Taylor was able to hit 71% of his throws for 360 yards and three scores, and Trinidad Chambliss should be able to do the same. In just five games, Chambliss has completed more passes than anyone else in the SEC, the deep shots are there, and … Missouri vs Ole Miss Prediction, Betting Lines Chambliss will have to get working, because his defense is about to have a long day against the Missouri running game. The Tigers have stepped it up on the ground over the last few weeks, and the Rebel defense is struggling against teams that keep on hammering away. But this will be way more of a firefight than Missouri is used to, and Chambliss and the Rebel offense will be far better in the fourth quarter of a back-and-forth fight. This will be a blast. The Rebels are coming off a dominant win over Vanderbilt, while the Tigers handled Texas A&M last week. This game features a quarterback reunion as former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons returns to Oxford. It should be a highly competitive matchup with massive stakes. Here are three bold Ole Miss predictions for Saturday's game. Kewan Lacy Goes Over 100 Rushing Yards Mississippi Rebels running back Kewan Lacy. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kewan Lacy returned to the lineup after a one-game absence against Florida and finished with seven carries for 39 yards. The superstar running back has yet to eclipse 100 rushing yards this year, but that changes on Saturday. Ole Miss desperately needs to revive its running game, but Missouri has been stout against the run. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards per game in the SEC (78.33). However, I think the Rebels will feed Lacy, and he'll make a statement against his former team. Ole Miss is built around Trinidad Chambliss, but Lacy plays just as big a role in this offense. It's time Lacy gets unlocked. The Ole Miss Defense Forces a Critical Takeaway Mississippi Rebels safety Nick Cull celebrates with cornerback Dante Core. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Rebels finally forced multiple takeaways last week. away.headline: Ex-Rebels QB lead No. 13 Missouri into Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss
away.blurb: Simmons, top receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. weren’t made available to speak Tuesday about transferring from Ole Miss, but it’s worth noting that Simmons’ Instagram account still has a number of posts from his years in Oxford. “I feel like those guys are definitely going to come out and play with a chip on their shoulder,” tailback Jamal Roberts said. “We definitely can let them guys handle that.” No. 9 Ole Miss reached the College Football Playoff semifinals a season ago with Trinidad Chambliss at quarterback after Simmons went down early with an injury and lost his starting job. Tigers coach Eli Drinkwitz acknowledged that the game will be a big deal for Simmons, along with two other Mizzou players imported from Ole Miss. Drinkwitz just wants them to keep perspective, considering about 20% of FBS players are transfers. “The biggest thing is to not make it bigger than it is,” Drinkwitz told reporters Tuesday. “There are great memories from there. I think everybody left there in a positive light on both sides.” “We talk about the joy of the journey,” Drinkwitz said. “That was a part of their journey that made them who they are right now. I don’t think there has to be a whole lot more to it than that.” Mizzou (5-1, 2-1 Southeastern Conference) comes in having won two straight home games against SEC foes, most recently 27-6 over Texas A&M on Saturday. The Tigers’ biggest win so far came against Florida, 45-17 on Oct. 3. Simmons has been terrific for the Tigers, ranking 11th in FBS in passing efficiency rating. He’s completing 65% of his passes, with 14 touchdowns and one interception in 165 attempts. “He’s playing as an experienced quarterback in a really good system,” Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said. Lee has scored five touchdowns while leading the Tigers with 42 receptions and 616 yards. He and Simmons may be transfers, but they’re already leaders at Mizzou, other players say. Roberts will be another focal point for Ole Miss. After putting together two straight games of 200-plus yards, he ranks first in the SEC and second nationally with 828 rushing yards. Mizzou’s top back a season ago, Ahmad Hardy, is recovering from an offseason gunshot wound. Golding said that Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) will have its hands full trying to tackle Roberts. “He has the most yards after contact right now, which is something that has been an issue for us on tape,” Golding said. With Chambliss continuing to rank as a Heisman Trophy contender and NFL prospect, Ole Miss routed Vanderbilt 52-17 on Saturday. The Rebels also have wins against ranked opponents LSU and Louisville. “They’re a total team,” Drinkwitz said. “We need to play our best, most complete game to even be in the game.” In Mizzou’s most recent road game, the Tigers blew a fourth-quarter lead and lost at Mississippi State. He was absent from the injury report ahead of the Missouri contest, making him available for the meeting with his former program. away.headline: Ahmad Hardy injury update: Star Missouri football RB not yet back in practice
away.blurb: Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz said that there currently is no change to the Mizzou football running back’s injury status during his press availability Tuesday, Oct. 13. Drinkwitz said that Hardy has not yet started a two-week ramp-up period that he needs to see for the running back to return to the field. Drinkwitz, as recently as last Tuesday, said that he’d provide an update as soon as one was available. But rumors began to swirl on various online platforms Monday night, including PowerMizzou at 247Sports and on Reddit, that Hardy may be close to a return to practice. Drinkwitz was again asked about Hardy’s current status on Tuesday. The message board poster has become quite popular for a string of Mizzou predictions over the past year, some of which have panned out. “If he practices, I promise, I'll tweet it out. I won't even give it to Pete (ESPN reporter Pete Thamel),” Drinkwitz said. “We'll just do it ourselves. So, again, I think it's going to be really important — I know everybody's excited about where we're at and all that good stuff. When he's available, I promise you we’ll be excited to use him. But that’s not the story right now. So, nothing new.” Mizzou has its idle week after the game against the Rebels. That technically means that if Hardy is able to return to practice sometime this week, he would be in a position to possibly return for Mizzou’s next game Oct. 31 at Arkansas. That quote blends a couple of niche references that require a lot of hours spent online to recognize. home.blurb: Simmons, top receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. weren’t made available to speak Tuesday about transferring from Ole Miss, but it’s worth noting that Simmons’ Instagram account still has a number of posts from his years in Oxford. “I feel like those guys are definitely going to come out and play with a chip on their shoulder,” tailback Jamal Roberts said. “We definitely can let them guys handle that.” No. 9 Ole Miss reached the College Football Playoff semifinals a season ago with Trinidad Chambliss at quarterback after Simmons went down early with an injury and lost his starting job. Tigers coach Eli Drinkwitz acknowledged that the game will be a big deal for Simmons, along with two other Mizzou players imported from Ole Miss. Drinkwitz just wants them to keep perspective, considering about 20% of FBS players are transfers. “The biggest thing is to not make it bigger than it is,” Drinkwitz told reporters Tuesday. “There are great memories from there. I think everybody left there in a positive light on both sides.” “We talk about the joy of the journey,” Drinkwitz said. “That was a part of their journey that made them who they are right now. I don’t think there has to be a whole lot more to it than that.” Mizzou (5-1, 2-1 Southeastern Conference) comes in having won two straight home games against SEC foes, most recently 27-6 over Texas A&M on Saturday. The Tigers’ biggest win so far came against Florida, 45-17 on Oct. 3. Simmons has been terrific for the Tigers, ranking 11th in FBS in passing efficiency rating. He’s completing 65% of his passes, with 14 touchdowns and one interception in 165 attempts. “He’s playing as an experienced quarterback in a really good system,” Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said. Lee has scored five touchdowns while leading the Tigers with 42 receptions and 616 yards. He and Simmons may be transfers, but they’re already leaders at Mizzou, other players say. Roberts will be another focal point for Ole Miss. After putting together two straight games of 200-plus yards, he ranks first in the SEC and second nationally with 828 rushing yards. Mizzou’s top back a season ago, Ahmad Hardy, is recovering from an offseason gunshot wound. Golding said that Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) will have its hands full trying to tackle Roberts. “He has the most yards after contact right now, which is something that has been an issue for us on tape,” Golding said. With Chambliss continuing to rank as a Heisman Trophy contender and NFL prospect, Ole Miss routed Vanderbilt 52-17 on Saturday. The Rebels also have wins against ranked opponents LSU and Louisville. “They’re a total team,” Drinkwitz said. “We need to play our best, most complete game to even be in the game.” In Mizzou’s most recent road game, the Tigers blew a fourth-quarter lead and lost at Mississippi State. Mandatory Credit: Ashley Tumlin-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 9:10 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 3 Miami looks unstoppable heading into its rivalry showdown with Florida State. Can the struggling Seminoles avoid another embarrassing defeat? One of college football's fiercest rivalries returns as No. 3 Miami (5-0) hosts Florida State (3-3) at Hard Rock Stadium. These two programs couldn't be heading in more different directions. Miami is coming off a dominant 41-13 victory over Clemson and remains firmly in the national championship conversation. Meanwhile, Florida State suffered an embarrassing 44-20 loss to Louisville after blowing an early 14-0 lead. With Miami entering as a heavy favorite, Mike Norvell and the Seminoles could be in serious trouble. Miami: The Hurricanes Look UNSTOPPABLE Mario Cristobal has built one of the most complete teams in college football, and quarterback Darian Mensah is playing like a legitimate Heisman Trophy contender. Mensah has thrown for 1,438 yards, 15 touchdowns, and zero interceptions this season. Miami is averaging an incredible 49.6 points per game while allowing just 9.8. Freshman sensation Malachi Toney has been nearly impossible to defend, recording 604 receiving yards and six touchdowns. His explosiveness gives Miami a dangerous weapon against a Florida State secondary that has struggled against quality competition. Running back Mark Fletcher Jr. provides another dimension to the offense, and Miami should have opportunities to establish the run against a vulnerable Seminoles defense. Florida State: Mike Norvell Is Running Out of Answers Florida State's season has quickly become a disappointment. The Seminoles allowed an unbelievable 397 rushing yards against Louisville, including 235 yards from Isaac Brown. That's a massive problem against Miami's balanced offense. Quarterback Ashton Daniels has thrown for 1,320 yards, eight touchdowns, and seven interceptions this season. Although Daniels has been dangerous with his legs, his inconsistency as a passer could become a serious issue against Miami's defense. Running back Ousmane Kromah has been productive with 565 rushing yards, but the Seminoles cannot rely entirely on their ground game if Miami builds an early lead. Florida State has enough athleticism to make some plays, but its defensive struggles and offensive turnovers make this an extremely difficult matchup. How Each Team Wins For Miami, the formula is simple: establish the run, protect the football, and allow Mensah to attack Florida State's secondary. Defensively, the Hurricanes must contain Daniels' rushing ability and force him to win from the pocket. For Florida State, everything starts with controlling possession. The Seminoles must establish Kromah, limit Miami's explosive plays, and create turnovers. If Florida State allows this game to become a shootout, it could get ugly quickly. I simply don't see Florida State having enough answers for Miami's offense. Mensah has been outstanding, and I expect him to continue his Heisman-caliber season against a Seminoles defense that just surrendered 44 points to Louisville. Florida State should create a few explosive plays with Daniels and Kromah, especially early, but Miami's defense will eventually take control. I expect the Hurricanes to establish a comfortable halftime lead before completely taking over in the second half. Final Score: No. 3 Miami 45, Florida State 20 Miami remains undefeated, improves to 6-0, and strengthens its national championship case. Sophomore Max Buchanan will be sidelined for an extensive portion of the season. He was injured in the Hurricanes' 41-13 win over Clemson at Death Valley (Memorial Stadium). Despite returning to finish the game, Buchanan underwent surgecal repairs. Given the Hurricanes' cross-training for offensive linemen, head coach Mario Cristobal will have a plethora of options. The big question: Who does he trust the most? It won't be revealed until kickoff, but here are candidates looking to take the starting role, plus a final prediction. After Buchanan initially went down against the Tigers, it was the fellow sophomore who stepped in. Alofaituli lost his starting role at left guard to freshman Max Buchanan. The 21-year-old logged 32 offensive snaps and finished with a 55 pass-protection Pro Football Focus grade. However, Alofaituli didn't allow a sack, pressure, hit, or hurry. He played the entirety of the Hurricanes' nine-play touchdown drive in the fourth quarter, which they exclusively ran the ball. However, Alofaituli doesn't have the traditional size for a guard. He's listed at 6-2 and 298 pounds. It's proven to be a weakness at times and the Seminoles could exploit if Alofaituli is lined up at right guard. It's been a slow freshman campaign for the former elite five-star recruit. Cantwell has logged just 78 offensive snaps through five games. As both starting tackle roles are occupied by veterans Samson Okunlola (left) and Matthew McCoy (right), the only real opportunities for the 18-year-old to play is in the interior. Cantwell has 59 snaps at right guard, but carving out a rotational role has been a different challenge. The Nixa (Mo.) native will very likely play at tackle as early as next season, but right guard is currently up for grabs. Cantwell could seize the moment, unless this final candidate has something to say about it. The Georgia transfer joined the Coral Gables program with experience all over the line of scrimmage, except center. Meriweather has played in a reserve role, but could be the closest to climbing the depth chart. In the Hurricanes' 52-3 win over Central Michigan, he logged 28 snaps and all were at right guard. Meriweather finished with an 83.3 pass-protection PFF grade. Similar to Cantwell, the redshirt junior is naturally a tackle, but he's shown comfortability in playing in the interior. Joining Okunlola, McCoy, and center Ryan Rodriguez at the line of scrimmage is Meriweather, educationally guessed by Roundtable Sports beat writer Anthony Aguirre. He has tremendous and versatile experience, which can benefit the Hurricanes' protection unit. picks.headline: Important Notes: No. 3 Miami Hurricanes Vs. Florida State Seminoles Preview, Injury Report, and More

Florida State Seminoles Preview, Injury Report, and More - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NHL Fantasy Hockey Stanley Cup Final World Juniors NBA Predictions World Series schedule Week 7 Waiver Wire 49ers are 6-0 Reese, Dream get even (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Anthony Aguirre Sat, October 17, 2026 at 1:24 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads MIAMI, Fla. – In less than 12 hours, the No. 3 Miami Hurricanes will kick off against the Florida State Seminoles for the 71st time in the Sunshine State's rivalry history. Both programs are powerhouses and multiple National Championship winners, but it's different this time around. The Seminoles have progressively declined since the 2023 13-1 season; meanwhile, the Hurricanes are on the brink of fully reclaiming former glory. Here is what's most important to know before Saturday night's game: Television Channel: ESPN Kickoff Time: 7:00 p.m. E.T. The Hurricanes are -2000 favorites to win and the Seminoles have a +1000 chance to pull off an upset. The spread is at -20.5 and the over/under is at 50.5. The following Hurricanes players are ruled out: Wide receiver Joshua Moore (Upper-Body; Out for Season), running back CharMar "Marty" Brown (Left Leg; Out for Season), cornerback Ja'Boree Antoine (Undisclosed), right guard Max Buchanan (Left Knee), cornerback Romans "OJ" Frederique Jr. (Left Shoulder), and tight end Luka Gilbert (Undisclosed; Out for Season). Junior cornerback Xavier Lucas is set to return from a four-game absence. Star edge rusher Marquise Lightfoot, linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin Jr., and cornerback Damari Brown were banged up ahead of the bye week, but aren't listed on the injury report. The following Seminoles are ruled out: Running back Samuel Singleton Jr., wide receiver Devin Carter, safety Karson Hobbs, linebacker Blake Nichelson, cornerback Jamari Howard, linebacker Izayia Williams, cornerback Jordan Crutchfield, and linebacker Daylen Green. Freshman linebacker Noah LaValle was listed as questionable on the initial injury report, but has been officially ruled out. Meanwhile, edge rusher Darryll Desir and center Paul Bowling are probable. The Seminoles have the second-most rushing attempts in the Atlantic Coast Conference; meanwhile, the Hurricanes have the best run defense in the Football Bowl Subdivision. Sophomore running back Ousmane Kromah is a great offensive threat. He's second in the ACC with 565 rushing yards on 100 carries and scored five touchdowns. Kromah is among the nation's leaders with 38 forced missed tackles. As the Hurricanes' front seven looks to be at full strength, the 20-year-old will meet with swarmers. Seminoles' fifth-year quarterback Ashton Daniels will need to dispute all early narratives this season. He has one of the lowest completion percentages (59.5) among ACC starters. The Hurricanes will likely look to force Daniels to throw more while simultaneously stopping the run – a similar game plan against Clemson and freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds. However, where Daniels lacks in passing, the 22-year-old makes up for on the gound. He leads the ACC with 10 rushing touchdowns. Defensive coordinator Corey Hetherman has a fair amount of experience in facing dual-threat quarterbacks and finding success. The Hurricanes have the highest-scoring offense (averaging 49.6 points) in FBS; meanwhile, the Seminoles have the 20th worst total defense. It should be a lopsided matchup at Hard Rock Stadium, but rivalrly games can get interesting. You could argue that the biggest surprise of the college football campaign is that Mike Norvell is still employed by Florida State . There is the whole $46.7 million buyout that looms, and the Seminoles are also searching for their next athletic director, but FSU seems destined for its third consecutive losing season and its fifth in Norvell's seven years in Tallahassee. The shouts for Norvell's axing are likely to get louder this week as the Seminoles travel to No. 3 Miami as 21.5-point underdogs before hitting their bye week. If Florida State is blown out for the second straight week, it could be curtains for Norvell. It is almost certainly delaying the inevitable, but I think the Seminoles may be able to avoid getting embarrassed at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday. I'm not saying that Florida State will win, or even make Miami sweat it out, but the Seminoles are competent enough to keep this thing within three scores. It's a low bar, I know. Games involving the Hurricanes have boasted an average spread of 32 points, and the Hurricanes have only faced one team ranked inside the top 50 of Bill Connelly's SP+ power rankings: Wake Forest. While the Hurricanes were still a comfortable 13-point road victor against the Demon Deacons, Wake Forest did cover the spread by seven points, and the box score suggests it may have deserved even better. Miami gained 5.6 yards per play, while Wake Forest averaged 5.4, thanks to 312 passing yards. For all of their warts, the Seminoles have started to build some momentum with the ball. They currently rank as the 35th-best offense in FBS, per SP+, and their 8.1 yards per pass is 41st in the country. Miami Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Nobody's writing home to grandma about those numbers, but they do suggest that Florida State has a real shot at keeping pace with Miami long enough to land us inside the number. And it's not just the aerial attack that gives me some optimism. There's also reason to believe that Florida State can be the first team this season to put a dent in Miami's elite run defense. QB Ashton Daniels has plenty of flaws, but he is a strong runner and is averaging 4.6 yards per carry and has 10 rushing touchdowns this season. His tailback, Ousmane Kromah, is on his way to a 1,000-yard campaign and is averaging 5.7 yards per rush. That's not a huge ask, but it will go a long way in making the Hurricanes at least a little uncomfortable on defense, something they haven't really had to deal with in 2026. Florida State is coming off a deflating loss to Louisville, but its two previous games against FBS opponents were more encouraging. The Seminoles hung with Alabama through three quarters and covered the spread on the road, and they crushed Virginia, 38-7, in Week 5. Those results, along with some of the numbers, tell us that there is a semi-competent team somewhere in this mess. We just need to hope that it shows up at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday. By Reice Shipley Contributing Sports Writer 0 Share Newsweek is a Trust Project member See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. The Florida State Seminoles came up just short in one of the best games of the 2026 college football season in a heartbreaking overtime loss to the Miami Hurricanes on Saturday night. Kromah was forced to exit early from Saturday's game after suffering an ankle injury. It was apparent right away that the injury appeared to be quite serious, as Kromah required a cart to get off the field. Unfortunately, the worst fears of Florida State fans were confirmed by CBS Sports College Football insider Matt Zenitz in a report on Kromah's status moving forward. More news : Oregon State WR Beats Ohio State’s Jeremiah Smith to Impressive Milestone According to Zenitz, Kromah is set to miss the remainder of the 2026 season due to his injury. More news : Controversial Officiating on Final Play of Notre Dame-BYU Game Sparks Outrage Kromah has essentially been the driving force for the Florida State offense this season, ranking as the third-leading rusher in the ACC this year. So while senior running back Quintrevion Wisner performed well in Kromah's absence, this certainly is a tough blow to a Florida State team that was just on the verge of their biggest win of the season. On the bright side, Florida State head coach Mike Norvell will get adequate time to put together a game plan moving forward without Kromah, as the Seminoles have a much-needed bye week in Week 8 before returning home in Week 9 to host the Clemson Tigers.

away.headline: Initial week 7 injury report for Florida State vs. No. 3 Miami could spell disaster for the Seminoles
away.blurb: Florida State needs some luck on its side to take down Miami, but that might not happen with multiple players notably absent from the initial injury report . The Hurricanes had two starters in particular suffer injuries last time out against Clemson, but neither player was included in the injury report, which means the Seminoles will be getting the best version of Miami in Week 7. DB Romanas Frederique Jr. (out) LB Noah LaVallee (questionable) No Lightfoot and no McCoy on the injury report likely means Florida State will be playing against a full-strength Miami team. The Hurricanes have a few players who have been ruled out for the game, but nothing serious has changed from last week. That could be an issue for the Seminoles, who already will face two serious mismatches in Week 7. The Hurricanes' offense could also receive a boost if McCoy avoids having to sit out the Week 7 game against the Seminoles. There is no two ways about it, Florida State has struggled to generate consistent pressure on opposing quarterbacks this season. The performance against Virginia in Week 5 was exceptional, but it should be viewed as the outlier at this point, with more disappointing performances than positive ones on defense. Florida State is just days away from perhaps the biggest game on the schedule against ACC rivals No. 3 Miami. The Hurricanes have displayed arguably the best offense and the best defense in the country this season, while the Seminoles have struggled to play consistent football. Starting edge rusher and Miami's sack leader, Marquise Lightfoot, left the game against Clemson early, but the star defender was not included in the first Week 7 injury report. Additionally, starting right tackle Matthew McCoy was attended to by the training staff against the Tigers, but ultimately played the rest of the game. McCoy was also not included in the initial Week 7 injury report for Miami. Marquise Lightfoot, Matthew McCoy left off Miami's initial injury report for the Florida State game For Miami, getting Lightfoot back would be tremendous due to how quickly he can create an impact on the field. Lightfoot disrupts offenses, and Florida State's best chance at igniting the offense is by giving the football to dynamic running back Ousmane Kromah. The running back has been the one constant this season for the Seminoles' offense, but he may meet his match against Lightfoot. Lightfoot currently has 20 total tackles and five sacks this season, with a sack in each of his last four games. The defender also recorded a sack and two tackles against Clemson before exiting, and while Miami has a lot of talent capable of filling the potential void, nobody creates quite as much chaos as Lightfoot does. It is going to be very hard for Florida State, a team that already struggles with generating pressure, to do so against a team like Miami, who have only allowed five total sacks this season. The Seminoles cannot win this game if quarterback Darian Mensah is given a clean pock

away.headline: Report: Florida State's Kromah out for season with foot injury
away.blurb: Report: Florida State's Kromah out for season with foot | theScore Sportsbook (opens in new tab) Casino (opens in new tab) theScore Download App Home Top News Kromah was carted off the field in the second quarter of Saturday's 43-35 loss to Miami and didn't return. The star running back tried to hop off the field after a 9-yard carry but fell to the turf before medical personnel put an air cast on his leg. Florida State running back Ousmane Kromah is expected to miss the rest of the season due to a foot injury, sources told CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz . Kromah has recorded 114 carries for 609 yards and five touchdowns this season. His 609 rushing yards rank third in the ACC, and he's posted two 100-yard rushing games this season. The sophomore initially committed to Georgia before flipping to Florida State. He rushed for 408 yards on 72 carries as a freshman in 2025. Quintrevion Wisner has the second-most carries (38) on Florida State behind Kromah this season. The Seminoles fell to 3-4 after the Miami loss and will face Clemson on Oct. 31 following their bye week. away.headline: Miami vs Florida State live updates: Hurricanes, Seminoles head to OT
away.source: The Palm Beach Post on MSN
away.blurb: Ashton Daniels kneeled out the clock, and we're headed to overtime. The teams will alternate possessions starting at the opponents' 25-yard line. If it goes to a second overtime, teams will have to go for 2 if they score a touchdown. After that, the teams will trade 2-point conversion tries until there's a winner. In his first game back since the opener at Stanford, cornerback Xavier Lucas made what could turn out to be the biggest play of the game. Tre Wisner got loose on a long run, but Ethan O'Connor stripped the ball loose, sending the ball skidding across the wet grass. Lucas fell on it to give Miami the ball at its own 39. Darian Mensah may not be having his best game, but he is still showing impeccable touch on some difficult throws. He got a throw out just before Rylan Kennedy could get to him, lofting a 19-yard looper to Vandrevius Jacobs. As the fourth quarter begins, the Canes have the ball at the FSU 20. Miami outgained FSU 149-76 in the third quarter, but the visitors benefitted big time on two turnovers (one on downs). UM can't afford to miss here if they want to stay undefeated. One play after Ousmane Kromah was carted to the locker room with a devastating ankle injury, Ashton Daniels took it in himself for the game-tying touchdown from 2 yards out. He held up three and two fingers to shout out Kromah's number 32 after the score. With FSU driving again and the 2-minute timeout having just passed, Chase Smith wrapped up Ousmane Kromah by the ankles. The running back was injured on the play, and trainers brought out an air cast for him. He was carted off the field. The Seminoles were already without Sam Singleton Jr. entering the game; without Kromah, among the top-20 running backs in the nation with 565 yards entering the game, Texas transfer Tre Wisner becomes their main RB. After a Miami three-and-out, Ashton Daniels returned to the game and looked like he didn't miss a beat, scrambling for 10 yards on a third-and-8. Later, he dumped a screen pass over three rushing Hurricanes to tight end Dessirio Riles for a 23-yard touchdown to tie it up. FSU is averaging 6.1 yards per play against a banged-up Miami defense. Ashton Daniels scrambled for 14 yards. As he slid, safety Zechariah Poyser hit him in the head area, bringing out a flag for the personal foul. His ejection for targeting was upheld upon review. That play and Bryce Fitzgerald's injury leaves an already depleted Miami secondary without two more starters. Xavier Lucas got injured in the opener vs. Stanford and hasn't played since, but he's expected to be back in the starting lineup tonight. O.J. Frederique also has been out since Week 1 but needs more time to return, leaving either Damari Brown, Ethan O'Connor or converted safety Bryce Fitzgerald starting opposite Lucas against FSU. AccuWeather predicts 80 degrees with thunderstorms possible at kickoff in Miami Gardens, Florida. Winds are expected to blow out of the north at 8 mph. There's about a 70% chance of rain and storm

Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 9:06 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 15 Kentucky travels to Norman after upsetting LSU, but Oklahoma's dominant defense could bring the Wildcats back down to earth. Two teams coming off massive upset victories will collide Saturday night as No. 15 Kentucky (5-1) travels to Norman to face Oklahoma (3-2) in a crucial SEC matchup. Kentucky is coming off a thrilling 35-34 overtime victory over LSU, while Oklahoma stunned Texas 27-24 in the Red River Rivalry. Both programs have plenty to prove, but the biggest question is whether Oklahoma can build on its impressive victory and finally establish some consistency. Kentucky: Can the Wildcats Keep Rolling? Kentucky has been one of the SEC's biggest surprises under first-year head coach Will Stein. Quarterback Kenny Minchey has thrown for 1,394 yards and 11 touchdowns, while running back CJ Baxter has rushed for 484 yards and eight scores. Baxter was outstanding against LSU, rushing for 123 yards and two touchdowns. The Wildcats are averaging nearly 35 points per game, but Oklahoma's defense presents a completely different challenge. Brent Venables has built one of the nation's most physical defensive units, allowing just 17.6 points and approximately 267 yards per game. If Kentucky cannot establish Baxter early, Minchey could face constant pressure throughout the evening. Oklahoma: The Defense Is Carrying This Team Oklahoma's victory over Texas was impressive, but the Sooners still have serious offensive concerns. Quarterback John Mateer has thrown for 1,038 yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Against Texas, Mateer managed just 155 passing yards, and Oklahoma needed a blocked punt touchdown and multiple defensive stops to secure the victory. However, the Sooners' defense has been outstanding. Oklahoma is allowing just 150 passing yards per game, making life extremely difficult for opposing quarterbacks. With Adepoju Adebawore creating pressure up front, the Sooners have the personnel to disrupt Kentucky's offense. If Mateer can avoid turnovers and Oklahoma establishes any consistency running the football, the Sooners should have enough offensive production to win. How Each Team Wins Kentucky must establish Baxter early, protect Minchey, and avoid giving Oklahoma short fields through turnovers. The Wildcats also need to force Mateer into obvious passing situations. For Oklahoma, everything starts defensively. The Sooners must contain Baxter, pressure Minchey, and create opportunities for their offense. Playing in Norman should also provide a significant advantage for Venables' team. I expect Kentucky to keep this game competitive, but Oklahoma's defense will ultimately make the difference. The Wildcats should find some success moving the football, particularly early, but sustaining long drives against this Sooners defense will be extremely difficult. Mateer won't need to deliver a spectacular performance. Instead, Oklahoma will rely on its defense, field position, and a few explosive offensive plays. Expect Kentucky to threaten late before Oklahoma comes up with one final defensive stop. Final Score: Oklahoma 27, No. 15 Kentucky 21 The Sooners build on their Red River victory, improve to 4-2, and keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive. It's just assumed that Texas will find its way into the College Football Playoff, and maybe get to the SEC Championship first. But it just lost to an Oklahoma team that pulled off an all-time found-a-way 27-24 win in the Red River Rivalry. The Sooners only have one SEC loss – 41-13 to Georgia – but all of a sudden, the second half of the schedule doesn't seem that bad. Kentucky, because it's in the first year of the Will Stein era, and Oklahoma, because it beat Texas – both programs are in a good place. But the winner of this will still be alive in the SEC, and the other almost certainly won't. Kentucky vs Oklahoma: Quick Hits Oklahoma goes on the road for two of the next three weeks, traveling to Mississippi State, hosting South Carolina, and going to Florida. It's a key stretch for Kentucky with Vanderbilt at home next, followed by a date at Tennessee. The two programs have only met three times. Oklahoma won 29-8 in 1982 and 29-7 in 1980, but Bear Bryant's Kentucky won the 1951 Sugar Bowl. Kentucky is No. 1 in the SEC in fewest penalties and fewest penalty yards, and that matters. The lack of turnovers matters. It all matters, because Oklahoma probably can't pull this off without the Wildcats royally screwing up like Texas did last week. Why Oklahoma Will Win Kentucky needs its running game to rock, and that's going to be a problem. Georgia was able to power away on Oklahoma with a few big runs in the blowout win, but that's been about it. Michigan tried to run a lot, and it did just enough to get by, but it was a struggle. Texas wasn't exactly creative in the way it tried to run, and it got stuffed way too often. The Sooners are 3-0 when they don't allow a touchdown run, and 0-2 when they do. Oklahoma will hold up defensively in a low-scoring game that comes down to a few key late stops, but this won't be easy for a team that failed to hit 300 yards of total offense against anyone but UTEP. Kentucky is 135th in the nation in third down conversions. Oklahoma is third in the nation in third down stops. And that's the ball game. picks.headline: No. 15 Kentucky at Oklahoma: KSR Staff Predictions
Kentucky Wildcats at Oklahoma Sooners Prediction, Picks & Odds for Week 7
How No. 15 Kentucky football & Oklahoma match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Having led Kentucky to back-to-back 35-34 overtime wins, Kenny Minchey is proving himself a cool customer under game-deciding stress. Two weeks ago at South Carolina, Minchey had running back CJ Baxter make a pre-snap shift so he could pick up an otherwise-free edge rusher. As the block was achieved, Minchey threw the game-winning two-point-conversion pass. Last week, Minchey realized the LSU defense had a Grand Canyon-sized hole in the middle of its formation. On a called pass play, the Hendersonville, Tennessee, product instead ran right through that hole for the game-winning two-point-conversion run. On the season, the 6-foot-2, 211-pound Minchey is completing 67.4% of his passes and has thrown for 1,394 yards with 11 touchdown throws vs. one interception. • Oklahoma’s John Mateer began the season on the outskirts of the Heisman Trophy discussion but has so far had a rough go in 2026. Ball security has been a problem for the 6-1, 224-pound Mateer. He threw a crucial interception late in Oklahoma’s 17-10 loss at Michigan in Week 2. He also turned the ball over three times in the first half at Georgia on Sept. 26, helping the Bulldogs open a 28-0 halftime lead en route to a 41-13 win. In Oklahoma’s 27-24 upset of then-No. 1 Texas last week, however, Mateer completed 18 of 26 passes for 155 yards with no interceptions. Mateer has not been as effective a rusher so far in 2026 as he has been in past seasons. Through five games, Mateer has a net-70 yards rushing. Advantage : Kentucky Running backs • Kentucky’s CJ Baxter ripped off a 77-yard run on UK’s first play from scrimmage in last week’s win over LSU. The 6-1, 230-pound product of Boynton Beach, Florida, finished with 123 rushing yards on 19 carries against the Tigers. A transfer from Texas, Baxter is fifth in the SEC in rushing with 484 yards. Third-year player Jason Patterson has carried only seven times combined in the past two games after suffering an apparent injury at South Carolina. A 5-10, 204-pound product of Sneads, Florida, Patterson had been one of UK’s breakout players over the season’s first four games. • Oklahoma’s ground game has, so far, been mostly stalled. The Sooners are last in the SEC in rushing, averaging only 95.8 yards a game. Lloyd Avant Jr ., a transfer from Colorado State who began his college career at Tulsa, leads the Sooners in rushing with 239 yards and two touchdowns on 52 carries (an average of 4.5 yards a rush). Avant, however, had a strong showing in the win over Texas, rushing 10 times for 72 yards and a touchdown. Wide receivers • Kentucky true freshman Kenny Darby was named SEC Freshman of the Week for the second straight week after catching four passes for 79 yards, including two crucial receptions late in the game, in the win over LSU. On the season, Darby, a 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, is eighth in the SEC in receptions (29) and ninth in receiving yards (401). Ja’Kayden Ferguson had caught only three total passes in UK’s first five games, but the 6-2, 184-pound, second-year player made three key receptions in the win over LSU. “He made some unbelievable plays,” Will Stein said of Ferguson. “... He blocked hard. He played hard. He’s got a lot of talent, a lot of upside.” • Isaiah Sategna III has been Oklahoma’s most effective offensive skill player so far in 2026. The 5-10, 185-pound senior from Austin, Texas, has 25 catches for 331 yards and two touchdowns. Sategna caught five passes for 64 yards in the win over Texas. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez made a team-high six catches for 25 yards vs. LSU. A 6-4, 249-pound junior from Covington Catholic, Rodriguez is second on the UK team in receptions (28) and receiving yards (219). Henry Boyer had a quiet showing vs. LSU with one catch for four yards. The 6-6, 270-pound transfer from Illinois has only nine catches on the season, but those receptions have yielded 120 receiving yards and three touchdowns. • Oklahoma’s Rocky Beers is, like UK’s Rodriguez, one of the best pass-catching tight ends in the SEC. A 6-5, 240-pound senior from Littleton, Colorado, Beers has 22 receptions for 284 yards and two touchdowns. Beers had four catches for 29 yards vs. Texas. Hayden Hansen caught 30 passes for 254 yards and two TDs last season while playing for Florida. So far this season, the 6-8, 270-pound Hansen has five catches for 74 yards and a TD. Advantage : Even Offensive line • After having a rough go against Alabama in Week 2, Kentucky right tackle Malachi Wood has consistently been playing solid football. “Malachi is a really-good football player,” Will Stein said. “The guy is 6-8, 330 pounds. He is gonna be, probably, a top three-round NFL draft pick in the next couple years. “ • The Oklahoma offensive front has been much-criticized amidst the Sooners’ offensive struggles, but the unit showed some signs of hope in the second half vs. Texas. Freshman Noah Best has emerged as the jack-of-all-trades on the OU offensive line, already logging starts this season at center and both guard positions. Defensive line • Kentucky nose guard Jamarrion Harkless was one of the unsung heroes of the win over LSU. The 6-3, 346-pound alumnus of Frederick Douglass High School made three tackles, 1.5 sacks, forced a fumble and had a quarterback hurry against Lane Kiffin’s Tigers. “I told (Harkless) ‘That’s how you have to play for us to be successful on defense, game in, game out,’” Will Stein said. • Oklahoma defensive tackle David Stone is an interior force. The 6-3, 312-pound junior from Del City, Oklahoma, made five tackles in the win over Texas. On the season, Stone has 19 tackles, two tackles for loss and half a sack. Advantage : Oklahoma • Due to injuries, Kentucky starting linebackers Grant Godfrey and Bo Barnes had to be iron men vs. LSU. WLB Barnes made 12 tackles and 2.5 tackles for loss, while MLB Godfrey made 10 stops vs. the Tigers. • Oklahoma MLB Owen Heinecke leads the Sooners in tackles (36), is tied for the team lead in quarterback hurries (two) and is second in tackles for loss (4.5). A 6-1, 226-pound fifth-year player from Tulsa, Heinecke made nine tackles vs. Texas. Defensive backs • Kentucky senior strong safety Ty Bryant made six tackles and intercepted a pass vs. LSU. For the 6-foot, 196-pound Bryant, a product of Frederick Douglass High School, it was his sixth career pick. Cornerback Terhyon Nichols made seven tackles and successfully defended a pass vs. LSU. • Oklahoma strong safety Peyton Bowen returned an interception of Texas quarterback Arch Manning 42 yards for a touchdown in the fourth quarter last week. A 6-foot, 200-pound product of Corinth, Texas, Bowen has made 24 tackles on the season, leads the Sooners in pass breakups with four and also has a forced fumble and a sack. Special teams • Kentucky punt returner Brock Coffman brought an LSU kick back 55 yards for a touchdown last week. Place-kicker Adam Zouagui entered last week’s game 6 of 7 on field-goal attempts but went only 2 of 4 vs. LSU. However, after missing two makeable field goals in the fourth quarter last week, Zouagui came back to hit a 33-yard field goal with 12 seconds left in the contest to tie the game at 27 and force overtime. After Murray State transfer Thomas O’Hara punted in UK’s first five games, the Cats turned to former starter Wilson Berry vs. LSU. On three punts, Berry averaged 40.1 yards and pinned LSU inside its 20-yard line once. • Oklahoma’s special teams are elite. Danny Okoye blocked a Texas punt last week that Dakoda Fields recovered in the Longhorns’ end zone for a touchdown. Isaiah Sategna III is second in the SEC in punt returning, averaging 18.57 yards a return. He had an 88-yard punt-return touchdown in the season opener vs. UTEP. Punter Jacob Ulrich is averaging 44.31 yards on 16 kicks and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line three times. Place-kicker Tate Sandell kicked a 47-yard field goal on the game’s final play to beat Texas last week. On the season, Sandell is 5 of 8 on field goals with a long make of 53 yards (which also came against Texas). The Oklahoma Sooners are coming off of a huge win over the Texas Longhorns at the Cotton Bowl in the Red River Rivalry. The Kentucky Wildcats are coming off a huge overtime win over LSU. Both teams are on a high but are looking to improve their records on Saturday night. So, does the team in Kentucky that's maybe at its best as a program get the win? Or does Oklahoma get another ranked win and get back into the College Football Playoff conversation? Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee : Oklahoma 20, Kentucky 17 This feels almost like the clock striking midnight for Kentucky here, as much as it does for me, who's lived the last two weeks dangerously. Both teams are coming in off super highs from last week. Oklahoma clipped Texas 27-24 on a walk-off field goal. Kentucky walked off LSU 35-34 in overtime, their second straight walk-off overtime win, going for two and getting it on the final play. Honestly, in a vacuum, I trust Kentucky QB Kenny Minchey more than I trust OU's John Mateer. But Minchey is going up against a very good Oklahoma defense, while Mateer has a more navigable task when he has the ball. I still don't see points a plenty here, but Oklahoma forces a key turnover late, and that's enough with the home crowd in Norman to get a close and resume-boosting win at the season's midpoint. Ryan Roberts, A to Z Notre Dame : Kentucky 21, Oklahoma 20 This could be one of the ugliest games on the schedule, with both teams struggling to find much offensive consistency. Oklahoma will have chances to pull away, but John Mateer’s chaotic style makes it hard to trust the Sooners to put together four clean quarters. Mateer can make spectacular plays, but mistakes and questionable decisions could give Kentucky the extra possessions it needs to hang around. Don't expect a shootout here. This game could come down to which team makes fewer costly mistakes in the fourth quarter. I'm buying a little bit of Kentucky magic in this one. Kenny Minchey comes through with a couple of clutch plays at the biggest moments, giving the Wildcats just enough offense to pull off a road upset. Kentucky might not look dominant, and it certainly won't be pretty, but this team finds a way to make things interesting when the game is on the line. Oklahoma has a chance to put the Wildcats away but can't quite finish the job, opening the door for Kentucky to steal a win in a close, low-scoring battle. Tyler Forness, A to Z Florida : Kentucky 21, Oklahoma 16 Will Stein has the Wildcats on a heater right now, and he's doing it with the two things you want in Kentucky's place: confidence and guts. He's won two games this season because the Wildcats went for two at the end, and that kind of belief in your team will go a long way in establishing a foundation for your program. Things are different for the Sooners, who are coming off of a fantastic win in Red River. Even so, John Mateer can't do much other than throw shock, and he did that brilliantly on the final drive against Texas. I don't think Mateer will change overnight, and the Wildcats will take advantage of him enough to win. Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama : Oklahoma 21, Kentucky 14 This game suddenly looks much better than it did a week ago after both Kentucky and Oklahoma pulled off massive upsets last weekend. Red River can always get wonky, but few expected OU to beat the number one team in the nation given how the offense has played. Will Stein's Wildcats have gone from quietly looking like a good football team to potentially being one of the conference's better teams after just one loss to Alabama and a last-minute OT win over LSU. The truth, however, is that OU may have found something more than just some Red River magic. This will be arguably the hardest test of the year for Kenny Minchey, and the battle of the brains between Brent Venables and Will Stein will be notable, but I think Oklahoma will get the job done. Justin Churchill, A to Z Oklahoma : Oklahoma 21, Kentucky 17 The Oklahoma Sooners are almost ready to kick off their first SEC night game (excluding CFP games) since 2024. And this one should be big, with both teams riding an insane high after huge wins. The Kentucky Wildcats will give OU's defense fits. It will happen, and I know my score prediction probably doesn't show that, but I have OU getting a few takeaways in this one. Kentucky is going to do a bunch of pre-snap stuff that's going to confuse you. They are very good at that, but Brent Venables has his unit locked in right now. OU will win this game once again through the defense and special teams, with some little moments here and there from the offense. away.headline: Mailbag: How will CJ Baxter, other injuries affect Kentucky's playoff outlook?

Vanderbilt is winless in SEC play, but Kentucky must still be on alert this week. This team needs a bye week to rest a variety of injuries, but I would be wary about holding anyone out against the Commodores who can play at other positions with less depth. The linebacker depth should be helped by the return of Alex Afari, but he did not play in Oklahoma, even after a judge made him eligible on Friday. away.headline: Oklahoma vs. Kentucky Injury Report: Sooners offensive line banged up
away.blurb: After initially being listed as questionable, Michael Fasusi and Heath Ozaeta, a pair of players who have started a number of games for the Sooners over the last two seasons, were downgraded to doubtful. They joined fellow offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis as doubtful. This comes after Head coach Brent Venables said Fasusi was "just about ready" to make his return on Tuesday. Well, it looks like we'll have to wait another week for Fasusi's return. With Fasusi, Ozaeta, and Pierre-Louis doubtful for Saturday, the Sooners will have another combination starting up front for the Sooners. Ryan Fodje will continue to start at left tackle with true freshman Noah Best at left guard. Jake Miakkula will be at center once again with E'Marion Harris at right tackle. That leaves right guard as the question mark. Peyton Joseph is probably the player coming off the bench to start for the Sooners. He's been a rotational player at guard this season, playing 47 snaps this season. Starting cornerback Eli Bowen has been ruled out for Saturday, putting Trystan Haynes in line to make his second straight start. For the Kentucky Wildcats , one of the most important names to watch ahead of Saturday's primetime affair is running back C.J. Baxter. Baxter joined Kentucky via the transfer portal from Texas. He's run for 484 yards and eight touchdowns at 5.6 yards per carry this season. He remains questionable for Saturday, and Pete Nakos of On3 says he'll be a game-time decision. It would be a big blow to the Wildcats, but they have capable runners behind him on the depth chart in Jason Patterson (361 yards, 7.7 yards per carry) and former Sooner Jovantae Barnes (140 yards, 6.1 yards per carry). Fasusi has missed the last four games after playing with a shoulder injury against UTEP. Ozaeta was banged up in warm-ups ahead of the Red River Showdown, but still played 59 snaps up front. One of them will leave Autzen Stadium with what could be a damaging second conference loss of the season. Oregon is coming off a 17-15 upset defeat at the hands of then-No. 21 UCLA in which coach Dan Lanning’s Ducks squad turned the ball over seven times and was successful just once on 13 third-down conversions. Nebraska had then-No. 7 Indiana on the ropes last week, only to watch as Hoosiers wide receiver Nick Marsh victimized them for two long touchdowns and a late 20-17 win over the Cornhuskers at Memorial Stadium. Raiola impressed in relief of Moore, guiding the Ducks past the Trojans, only to struggle mightily in his first start with Oregon, throwing for just 43 yards (6-of-19) and two interceptions. Thomas replaced the wildly inefficient Raiola in the fourth quarter and accounted for 156 of the team’s 272 total yards on the day. If Raiola gets the starting nod under center, he’ll be facing his former team in Nebraska, where he passed for 4,819 yards and 31 touchdowns. Whoever starts for Lanning’s squad will stare across the line at a Huskers’ defense that has simply been dominant. Nebraska is allowing just 15.2 points and 276.2 yards per game with the nation’s best third-down defense (19.7 percent), ahead of No. 2 Oregon (22.1 percent). The Ducks must support Raiola or Thomas with an established run game, something that’s been lacking in Oregon's offense, which has yet to produce a 100-yard rushing performance from either running backs Jordon Davison or Dierre Hill Jr. They’ll have to do so against a Nebraska rush defense that ranks No. 17 in the country versus the run at 94.7 yards per game. The senior has been unstoppable of late with two of his team-high five sacks coming last week against the Bruins, along with a blocked field goal attempt. Nebraska quarterback Anthony Colandrea has been sacked 10 times this season, giving Uiagalelei and the Ducks an opportunity to exploit Nebraska’s protection issues. From there it’s just a matter of time for the tenacious Uiagalelei, who has four career forced fumbles, including a big one against Texas Tech in the 2026 Orange Bowl. picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska football is hitting the road for one of its biggest games of the season, and Adam Carriker is breaking it all down on the Carriker Chronicles! Matt Rhule and the Nebraska Cornhuskers are heading to Eugene to face Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks in a late-night Big Ten showdown. Both teams are coming off losses, and both have plenty to prove. Can the Huskers bounce back and pull off an upset? Nebraska enters the game at 5-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Curt Cignetti and Indiana. The Huskers showed some good things against the Hoosiers, but once again, they couldn't finish the job. Carriker discusses why Nebraska needs more than another moral victory. At some point, the Huskers have to start winning these big games, especially against talented Big Ten opponents. One of the biggest questions is whether Anthony Colandrea and Nebraska's offense can get things going against Oregon's defense. Colandrea has shown he can make plays, but Carriker believes offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen needs to put him in good situations, especially on third downs. The Huskers also need production from Jamal Rule and the running back rotation. Can Nebraska establish a running game and keep Oregon's defense guessing? On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's Blackshirts face a major challenge. Oregon has talented receivers who can stretch the field and create explosive plays. Carriker looks at Nebraska's defensive numbers and explains why the Huskers cannot allow Oregon to make big plays over the top. The Blackshirts have been improving, but this will be another serious test of just how far they've come. Carriker also breaks down Oregon's defense, including players like Matayo Uiagalelei and Bear Alexander. The Ducks have plenty of talent, but Oregon has also been unpredictable this season. Nebraska cannot afford to let this become the game where everything suddenly clicks for Oregon. This is also Nebraska's stiffest road test so far this year. Playing in Eugene, in front of a loud Oregon crowd, will test the Huskers' experience and mental toughness. Nebraska has added veteran players who have been through big games before. Now it's time to see whether that experience pays off. Carriker shares his four keys to the game: handle Oregon's crowd, execute in the red zone, prevent big plays and play all four quarters. Nebraska must protect Colandrea, finish drives and avoid the mistakes that have cost the Huskers in close games. Finally, Carriker discusses the point spread and makes his score prediction! He's picking Nebraska to pull off the upset, 24-21! Can Matt Rhule and the Huskers shock Oregon, earn their third Big Ten win and make a statement to the rest of college football? Or will Dan Lanning and the Ducks send Nebraska home with another disappointing loss? Get Adam Carriker's full Nebraska-Oregon preview, breakdown and prediction on the Carriker Chronicles! Stay up to date on all things Huskers by bookmarking Nebraska Cornhuskers On SI , following us on Twitter/X , and visiting HuskerMax.com daily. Loading recommendations... Please wait while we load personalized content recommendations ADAM CARRIKER Adam’s dream of playing for the Huskers came to fruition. He was twice named first-team All-Big 12, leading the conference in sacks and winning the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year award his senior season, along with several other awards, including finishing with All-America honors, in addition to being named to the Big 12 Commissioner’s Academic Honor Roll three times. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He was drafted in the 1st round, winning Rams Rookie of the Year; he’s the only Ram in franchise history to start all 16 games as a rookie. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. Since retiring, he’s experienced great success in the business world and has also appeared multiple times on National Television and Radio Shows, and currently hosts his highly popular show, the Carriker Chronicles, aka, the People’s Show, which has been viewed by millions!
