This is the season for an Oregon team that should be in full rock-and-roll mode at this point, but instead it's been one big, sad trombone of a season. The Ducks are still 3-2 with a not-that-horrible schedule the rest of the way outside of a trip to Ohio State. They lost to UCLA, but they can stay alive in the Big Ten title hunt with one more loss, even if an at-large CFP bid is likely gone with a third defeat and no Big Ten Championship. And they have to do it with Nebraska's former star quarterback, Dylan Raiola – maybe. Nebraska had Indiana cooked, but it turned the stove off too early. The Hoosiers rallied back for a 20-17 win, but that might have been more about the defending national champs not being as good this year than the Huskers being close to fantastic. However, winning in Eugene is still hard, and if Nebraska can do it, it's 6-1 with a favorable schedule – Ohio State comes to Lincoln – and all of a sudden, it's on the fast track to 10-2 – at least – and a possible at-large CFP bid. Nebraska vs Oregon: Quick Hits Oregon ends a good run of home games and goes to Illinois after this. After that, it hosts Northwestern before going to Ohio State. Nebraska starts a run of three road games in four dates, getting a week off before playing Washington, and then it's off to Illinois. The two have never played as Big Ten teams. Oregon won the last meeting 42-35 in 2017. The Huskers are 6-2 overall in the series, with the first win in 1952. How To Watch Nebraska vs Oregon Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 11:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Autzen Stadium, Eugene, OR – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Nebraska Will Win UCLA beat up, battered, and bruised Oregon last week. The Ducks might have knocked out Bruin quarterback Nico Iamaleava with a knee injury, but they were destroyed offensively with seven turnovers and just 272 yards of total offense. Oregon is a mess. Star quarterback Dante Moore is expected to miss another game after suffering a concussion against USC. Dylan Raiola might get his shot against his former team, but he was beyond awful against UCLA. Brock Thomas doesn't have Raiola's talent, but he got the offense moving in the second half. Nebraska gave up two huge touchdowns against Indiana, but held firm the rest of the way. Oregon's offensive problems won't all of a sudden be fixed this week. It's been the only team able to stuff the Bruin running game, and it should do the same against Nebraska, starting by keeping quarterback Anthony Colandrea from doing much on the move. The Huskers can force takeaways – three against Michigan State, two against Maryland – but the Ducks are capable of getting their running game moving a bit to take the pressure off the passing game. And about the quarterback situation, yes, Bob Chesney and the UCLA defense pitched a gem last week. But the week before that, Raiola stepped in and threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns in a brilliant fill-in performance for Moore against USC. Nebraska vs Oregon Prediction, Betting Lines This is too fluid to be definitive – Oregon might rotate quarterbacks no matter who starts – but this will be more on the Duck defense. It'll be fantastic against the Nebraska running game, and that will be enough. Oregon is 3-0 when allowing fewer than 140 yards on the ground, and Nebraska managed just 128 against Indiana. This won't be pretty, but it'll be a fascinating late-night battle with a few more points than you might expect. Now the Huskers travel up to Oregon for a 10 p.m. CT matchup, the latest start time for Nebraska since 2014. But other factors in this game make this clash all the more questionable. Dante Moore is out for the game, meaning Dylan Raiola, Brock Thomas or even Akili Smith Jr. will be earning the start. But Raiola is the most poetic option after all and is likely the starter despite a rough outing against UCLA. After going 19-of-25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns against USC, Raiola only threw 6-of-19 for 43 yards and two interceptions against the Bruins . He also got strip-sacked in the game. Though it was Raiola's only sack, UCLA still brought the pressure throughout. Raiola's main weakness is pressure, which the Bruins exploited last week. Though Raiola can find ways to stay alive in the pocket and deliver big plays, he rarely takes off downfield and has found himself in rough spots. Thomas took over in the fourth quarter for the Ducks and went 11-of-15 for 156 yards and a touchdown. He did, however, fumble on his opening drive but nearly completed the comeback. But even if Thomas starts, it remains to be seen whether he can replicate that success, especially after seeing Raiola's two-game stretch. Now, Nebraska can get to the quarterback, but the concern comes down to the explosive plays. Indiana pulled off multiple explosive plays last week, despite its struggle to produce points and yardage for most of the game. The Ducks can do the same, especially late in the game. Nebraska ran out of steam in the fourth against Indiana at home early in the afternoon. Now, the Huskers face Oregon on the road after dark. The Ducks almost completed their 17-6 comeback against UCLA, so they can find a way to do the same against Nebraska if needed. The Huskers' defense also needs to be cautious with Oregon's rushing game. Though the Ducks don't strike primarily on the ground, Dierre Hill Jr. and Jordon Davison combined for 216 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 54 carries over the last two games, averaging four yards per carry. Though UCLA did suffocate Oregon's run at times, Nebraska could let a play slip by if it's not careful. Oregon's defense also needs to be cautious, seeing how its last two games panned out. The Ducks held USC to 27 points, but Jayden Maiava still threw for 326 yards and two touchdowns on just 23 completions. Oregon also surrendered 205 passing yards on just 13 completions to UCLA, despite holding it to 17 points. Nebraska could do some damage on the run, however. Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker tallied 109 rushing yards earlier this season against the Ducks. Anthony Colandrea could do the same and help the Huskers score. Jamal Rule, Mekhi Nelson and Isaiah Mozee all could have moments as well after UCLA's Wayne Knight found some holes in Oregon's defensive line. Knight finished with 103 yards on 22 carries. But this game is also make-or-break for Oregon's postseason hopes, especially with Ohio State and even Northwestern coming up. The Ducks also have a talented roster and, despite their issues, can deliver major blows to opponents when momentum is on their side. Nebraska's issues on the line, in the secondary and even a bit on special teams don't help either. All of this, plus the after-dark setting, provides just enough to tip the scales in the Ducks' favor. Unless Nebraska can truly come out and play like a team that can earn a top-25 spot, this matchup will likely be another so-close-but-so-far loss. Game preview, prediction, betting line - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NBA Predictions World Series schedule Week 7 Waiver Wire 49ers are 6-0 Reese, Dream get even Ryan Clarke Fri, October 16, 2026 at 2:23 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oregon Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) seek to recapture momentum in what has been a massively disappointing 2026 season so far, and they'll have no time to rest and regroup as confident Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) comes to town. The Cornhuskers are coming off a highly competitive effort in a loss to defending national champions Indiana, while the Ducks have a quarterback battle to work out with Dante Moore still sidelined as he recovers from a concussion. Here is a preview: Oregon (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) vs. Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) When: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 8 p.m. PT Where: Autzen Stadium Latest line: Oregon by 7 Radio: Oregon Sports Network Stream : You can watch this game live with Fubo (free trial), or with DIRECTV (free trial). If you are out of free trials, you can also watch this game with Sling (cheapest streaming plans that include live sports). Streaming broadcasts for this game will be available on these streaming services locally in Oregon and Washington, but may not be available outside of the Pacific Northwest, depending on your location. LOOKING FOR REVENGE? Dylan Raiola will have to earn the opportunity to face his former team in Nebraska. A two-year starter for the Cornhuskers, Raiola has faced external criticism for his decision to transfer to Oregon, but he maintains a strong relationship with Nebraska coach Matt Rhule and several of his former teammates. Raiola's performance against UCLA last week was one of the worst by an Oregon quarterback in recent memory: 6 of 19 passing, 43 yards and two interceptions. This, just two weeks after a highly effective outing in relief of the injured Moore against USC. Raiola was pulled in the fourth quarter against UCLA in favor of Brock Thomas, who almost led a Ducks comeback. Akili Smith Jr. was apparently part of the quarterback competition this week, too. While it is far from a guarantee that Raiola will lead the Oregon offense out onto the field against Nebraska, his personal motivation could be enough to sharpen his focus and help earn him the chance — and perhaps bounce back in a big way performance-wise to lead the Ducks to victory. GETTING A PUSH Whether Raiola or any of the Oregon quarterbacks succeeds depends heavily on the men up front. Oregon's offensive line was dreadful last week after getting a strong push to establish the run just two weeks prior against USC. If the Ducks can't find balance and give Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill a chance to break off big plays, it will be a long day for whoever is tossing the pigskin for the Ducks and staring down Nebraska's edge rushers. Especially with top Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart listed as doubtful as of Thursday evening. Dan Lanning admitted this week that Oregon is still working out who its best five offensive linemen are. For a program that came into the season with major questions at the position and an entire spring and fall camp to figure those things out, that is a very bad sign. A MOBILE THREAT Nebraska quarterback Anthony Colandrea is a talented athlete who can make things happen with his legs. He will provide the biggest test yet for Oregon's front seven in containing a mobile quarterback, one they failed when facing Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker but largely passed against USC's Jayden Maiava. For all the bad that showed up in Oregon's befuddling, 17-15 loss to UCLA last week, the defense played well for the most part. Save for a deep pass on the first play of the game and Wayne Knight's touchdown run in the second quarter, the Ducks looked like the defensive line unit many expected them to be coming into the season. This Saturday, maintaining that level of play will start and end with keeping Colandrea in check. away.headline: 4 bold predictions as Oregon football looks to rebound vs. Nebraska
away.blurb: For Oregon: The good news for Oregon is seemingly, no player suffered a substantial injury in its loss to UCLA last weekend. The bad news is several key contributors were listed as out, including quarterback Dante Moore, with no clear timetable for return. Starting safety Aaron Flowers was also listed as out and Jeremiah McClellan sat with an injury sustained during warmups against Portland State. McClellan is expected to miss much of the season while Moore (concussion) and Flowers' status will be more clear Wednesday. For Nebraska: The Cornhuskers may face the Ducks without one of their best defensive backs in Jamir Conn, who left Nebraska's loss against Indiana with a chest injury and was seen in a sling on the sideline. Key defensive lineman Riley Van Poppel was listed as questionable through the week heading into the game but sat out the loss, as well. It's unclear whether either of those players will be ready to go against the Ducks. Let it be known that Lanning doesn't allow any outsiders at practice. We can only make predictions based on what we've seen in games and what coaches and athletes tell us, so our guess is as good as anyone's who follows along. But if Dante Moore is still recovering from his concussion and is held out against Nebraska this weekend, Dylan Raiola gives Oregon the best chance to win, at least from the onset. Raiola started 22 games for the Cornhuskers before transferring to Oregon and is a former five-star prospect with all the right tools to succeed. He threw for nearly 300 yards and two touchdowns against USC before an absolute stinker against UCLA. Though Brock Thomas gave the Ducks life in the fourth quarter, we think Raiola will get the first nod again, with a much shorter leash if things turn sideways. home.headline: Coach Bret Bielema divulges how injuries reshape Oregon vs. Illinois
home.blurb: Moore missed the last two games, but has participated in practice during those two weeks. Lanning continues to express that the program is handling his return to the active roster with care, but hasn’t yet ruled him out against the Illini. The first injury report is set to be released on Wednesday at 5 p.m. PT. While the Fighting Illini will be without their starter, Bielema faces the challenge of not knowing which opposing quarterback to prepare for. Moore could make his return on the road, or former walk-on Brock Thomas could start for the second consecutive game. Oregon could also let Dylan Raiola pick up where he left off against the Cornhuskers. Raiola has more experience of the two if Moore is unavailable. He has six touchdowns and 515 yards on 64.4 percent completion in 2026, while also having two years of starting experience at Nebraska under his belt, with 2,000-plus passing yards in each of those seasons. Two of the Oregon Ducks’ first five games of the 2026 season came on the road. Following their bye week and two straight games at Autzen Stadium, the Ducks now prepare to fly to the Midwest to take on the Illinois Fighting Illini. Oregon and Illinois played in Eugene in 2024 during the Ducks’ first season in the Big Ten. Oregon won that matchup 38-9, but will play in Champaign for the first time as members of the same conference. Ahead of the Week 8 showdown, Fighting Illini coach Bret Bielema reacted to the challenge of preparing for three different Oregon quarterbacks and acknowledged the quarterback injuries plaguing the Big Ten. Big Ten Quarterback Injuries Impacting Both Teams Bielema opened up by talking about Oregon, showing his respect for coach Dan Lanning and the Ducks’ program. “Obviously, Oregon (played) in a four-quarter game on Saturday,” Bielema said. “I made it til half, and knew I was going to watch that game a lot. But obviously, a lot of respect for Dan and his staff and his program and what they’ve been able to accomplish.” Bielema spoke about the similarities between Illinois and Oregon in the sense that they are both dealing with injuries to their starting quarterbacks. Dante Moore sustained a concussion against the USC Trojans on Sept. 26, ultimately heading to the hospital before returning to Eugene with the team. Meanwhile, Illinois senior quarterback Katin Houser is expected to miss four to six weeks following a procedure to his throwing hand. “I think they’ve kind of experienced the same things in the weekend. Katin (Houser) got hurt,” Bielema said. “There were three or four teams around the league that lost their potential No. 1 guy for a certain part of time. Part of college football that we’re seeing now, and I think the biggest thing for us is take advantage of the moment.” To Bielema’s point, Oregon’s most recent loss to the now-ranked No. 9 UCLA Bruins saw starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava exit with an injury. home.blurb: Multiple local outlets, including KATU's Hallie DeVore as well as KVAL , reported that Oregon star receiver Evan Stewart was booked at Springfield Municipal Jail on Sunday morning following the comeback victory over Nebraska on Saturday. Stewart, a senior, was ruled out for the game due to injury. Victim Information System in Oregon ( VISOR ) records showed Stewart was booked but out of custody. There is no official comment as of Monday morning from Stewart, Lanning, nor the University of Oregon. Here is more ( via ESPN ): "Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was arrested early Sunday on a charge of driving under the influence of intoxicants. Police in Springfield, Oregon, told local ABC affiliate KATU that Stewart was booked at approximately 7 a.m. PT on Sunday. Stewart was released about an hour later to a third party, fellow Oregon receiver Dakorien Moore, according to KATU." Other reporting indicates that Stewart's driving under the influence of intoxicants had nothing to do with "online rumors" of street racing involving other teammates ( via OregonLive.com ): "Springfield Police told The Oregonian/OregonLive on Sunday that online rumors of street racing involving Oregon football players were unfounded, and that several Oregon players were contacted by police early Sunday morning because they were in the area of a separate pursuit. That pursuit, which resulted in Springfield Police discovering an abandoned vehicle, was unrelated to Stewart's alleged DUII arrest. Springfield PD is no longer pursuing the case involving the abandoned vehicle, an official said." Springfield Police Department told USA TODAY's Ducks Wire that they "had no reason to believe" the car pursuit that evening was connected to the Oregon football team.
